title: ORGANIC LAW N° 001/2026.OL OF 25/02/2026 DETERMINING THE FUNCTIONING OF THE SENATE

articles.heading: Purpose of this Organic Law
Senate
Procedures for election or appointment of a Senator The election or appointment of a Senator is
articles.text:
effected in accordance with the provisions of
the Constitution of the Republic of Rwanda
and other Laws.

articles.heading: Responsibilities of the Senate (1) The Senate has the following responsibilities
articles.text:
(a) to debate laws, pass laws and legislate;
33
(b) to exercise oversight over Government
activities.
(2) The Senate also has the following
exclusive responsibilities:
(a) to monitor the application of the
following fundamental principles
provided for under the Constitution of
the Republic of Rwanda:
(i) the prevention and punishment
of the crime of genocide, fight
against denial and revisionism of
genocide as well as eradication
of genocide ideology and all its
manifestations;
(ii) the eradication of discrimination
and divisionism based on
ethnicity, region or on any other
ground as well as promotion of
national unity;
(iii) equitable power-sharing;
(iv) building a State governed by the
rule of law, a pluralistic
democratic Government,
34
equality of all Rwandans and
between men and women which
is affirmed by women occupying
at least 30% of positions in
decision-making organs;
(v) building a State committed to
promoting social welfare and
establishing appropriate
mechanisms for equal
opportunity to social justice;
(vi) the constant quest for solutions
through dialogue and consensus.
(b) to monitor the functioning of political
organisations;
(c) to provide the Chamber of Deputies
with its opinions on the budget
framework paper and on the draft law
determining State finances prior to its
final adoption.
35

articles.heading: Powers of the Senate (1) In legislative matters, the Senate is competent to vote on  (a) the revision of the Constitution of
articles.text:
the Republic of Rwanda;
(b) organic laws;
(c) laws approving the ratification of
international treaties and
agreements on –
(i) armistice;
(ii) peace;
(iii)modification of national
laws;
(iv) status of persons;
(v) establishment of an
international
organisation.
(d) laws approving accession of
Rwanda to international treaties
and agreements on international
organisation;
36
(e) laws on defence and national
security.
(2) The Senate is also vested with the power
to:
(a) approve the appointment of officials
provided for under the Constitution of
the Republic of Rwanda and other
Laws;
(b) provide advice on matters of major
national importance within its
responsibilities.

articles.heading: Offices incompatible with that of Senator (1) The office of Senator is incompatible with being
Resignation from office incompatible with that of Senator Except for the offices specified in Paragraph
articles.text:
(1)(f)(g)(h)(p) of Article 6 of this Organic
Law, the holding of any other office that is
incompatible with that of a Senator does not
preclude the holder thereof from being
elected or appointed as a Senator. Upon
taking the oath of office, however, such a
Senator forthwith resigns, in writing, from
the office previously held and informs the
President of the Senate and the Ombudsman
thereof.

articles.heading: Oath-taking and assumption of office by a Senator Before assuming office, a Senator takes, publicly before the President of the Republic
articles.text:
or, in the absence of the President, before the
President of the Supreme Court, the oath of
office provided for under the Constitution of
the Republic of Rwanda.

articles.heading: Term of office of Senator (1) An elected or appointed Senator serves 40 for a term of five years, renewable once
articles.text:
(2) A Senator who is a former Head of State
is not subject to the limitation on the
number of terms of office.

articles.heading: Declaration of assets Every Senator submits a written declaration of assets to the Office of the Ombudsman in
articles.text: accordance with the relevant legislation.

articles.heading: Vacancy in the office of Senator The office of a Senator becomes vacant when he or she – (a) resigns;
articles.text:
(b) is removed from office pursuant to a
court decision;
(c) is permanently unable, for any
reason whatsoever, to discharge his
or her functions; or
(d) dies.
41

articles.heading: Resignation from office of Senator A Senator who resigns from office of Senator tenders his or her letter of resignation to the
articles.text:
President of the Senate who, within seven
days of receiving the resignation letter,
informs the President of the Republic, the
Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies and the
President of the Supreme Court thereof. Such
resignation is also brought to the knowledge
of the population through an announcement
in the media and on the website of the Senate.

articles.heading: Replacement of Senator (1) Where an elected Senator ceases to hold office on any of the grounds provided for
articles.text:
under this Organic Law, he or she is
replaced in accordance with the
provisions of the Organic Law
governing elections. In the case of an
appointed Senator, the organ having
appointed him or her designates his or
her successor.
(2) Where a Senator ceases to hold office,
the President of the Senate, within 30
days, requests the organ having
appointed him or her or, in the case of an
42
elected Senator, the National Electoral
Commission, to replace him or her.
(3) A new Senator who is so elected or
appointed serves for the remainder of his
or her predecessor’s term of office. He
or she may be re-appointed or re-elected
for a further term of office.
CHAPTER II: ORGANISATION OF
THE SENATE

articles.heading: Organs of Senate (1) The organs of the Senate are the following
Members of the Plenary Assembly The Plenary Assembly comprises all Senators
articles.text: Section 2: Conference of Chairpersons

articles.heading: Members of the Conference of Chairpersons The Conference of Chairpersons comprises the members of the Bureau of the Senate and
articles.text:
the members of the Bureaus of Standing
Committees.
Section 3: Bureau of the Senate

articles.heading: Members of the Bureau of the Senate The Bureau of the Senate comprises a President and two Vice Presidents elected
articles.text:
from among the members of the Senate. One
44
Vice President is responsible for
parliamentary affairs and the other for
administration and finance.

articles.heading: Election of and oath-taking by members of the Bureau of the Senate (1) At the commencement of each new term
articles.text:
of office of Senators, the first sitting of
the Senate is devoted to electing the
Bureau of the Senate. Such sitting is
convened and presided over by the
President of the Republic within 30 days
of the final declaration of election results
of the elected Senators.
(2) The election of the members of the
Bureau of the Senate is by secret ballot
and determined by an absolute majority
of the votes of the Senators present at the
sitting. Each member of the Bureau of the
Senate is elected in a separate ballot.
Where no candidate for membership of
the Bureau secures the required number
of votes, the ballot is repeated.
(3) Failing an absolute majority of the votes
at the second ballot, the candidate with
the most votes is deemed elected.
(4) Before assuming office, the members of
45
the Bureau of the Senate publicly take,
before the President of the Republic, the
oath of office provided for under the
Constitution of the Republic of Rwanda.
(5) Members of the Bureau of the Senate
serve for a term of five years.
Section 4: Standing Committees

articles.heading: Standing Committees The Senate has the following four Standing Committees
Members of, and procedures for their assignment to, Standing Committee (1) Each Standing Committee comprises at
articles.text:
least four members.
(2) Senators are assigned to the Standing
Committee according to the following
procedures:
(a) every Senator registers with only one
Standing Committee;
(b) the Bureau of the Senate verifies the
registrations made by Senators and
confirms membership of each
Standing Committee having regard to
the following criteria:
(i) the preference expressed by each
Senator;
(ii) the number of members of each
Standing Committee;
(iii) the responsibilities of the
Standing Committee;
(iv) the relevance of the Senator’s
qualifications to the
responsibilities of the Standing
47
Committee;
(v) the Senator’s professional
experience in relation to the
functions of the Standing
Committee;
(vi) the principle of gender equality.
(3) After the expiry of a period of two and a
half years, a Senator who so wishes may
request a change in his or her Committee
membership. Such a request is considered
in the manner provided for under
Paragraph (2) of this Article.
(4) The Bureau of the Senate may, in the
interest of the service, reassign a Senator
from one Standing Committee to another.

articles.heading: Bureau of the Standing Committee and its election (1) Each Standing Committee has its own bureau consisting of a chairperson and a
articles.text:
vice chairperson.
(2) The chairperson and vice chairperson of
the Standing Committee are elected by
the Plenary Assembly by an absolute
48
majority of the votes of Senators present
at the plenary sitting. Members of the
Standing Committee wishing to be
elected inform the President of the Senate
in writing thereof who, in turn, informs
the Plenary Assembly thereof.
(3) The chairperson and the vice chairperson
of the Standing Committee are elected in
separate ballots.
(4) Where no candidate for membership of
the Bureau of a Standing Committee
secures the required number of votes, the
ballot is repeated.
(5) Failing an absolute majority of votes at
the second ballot, the candidate with the
most votes is deemed elected.

articles.heading: Term of office and procedures for replacement of members of the bureau of the Standing Committee
articles.text:
(1) Members of the bureau of the Standing
Committee hold office for a renewable
term of two and a half years.
(2) One or both members of the bureau of
the Standing Committee may be
replaced upon resignation or at the
49
request of two-thirds of the members of
the Standing Committee. A written
notice of resignation or calling for
replacement is addressed to the
President of the Senate.
(3) At the request of two-thirds of the
members of the Standing Committee,
the President of the Senate refers the
matter to the Committee for
consideration.
(4) A report of the Standing Committee
following its consideration of the matter
regarding the replacement of the bureau
or any of its members is presented to the
Plenary Assembly within a period not
exceeding seven days for decision.
(5) Where the bureau of the Standing
Committee or any of its members
resigns, or where the Plenary Assembly
decides to replace him or her, the
replacement is effected in the manner
provided for under Article 21 of this
Organic Law within 15 days of the date
on which the resignation is delivered to
the President of the Senate or of the
Plenary Assembly’s approval of their
replacement.

articles.heading: Establishment of Ad Hoc 50 Committee At the request of the President of the Senate
articles.text:
made after consultation with the other
members of the Bureau of the Senate, or at
the request of at least five Senators subject to
the approval of the Plenary Assembly, the
Senate establishes an ad hoc committee
tasked with considering a Draft Law or
Private Member’s Bill or any specific matter.

articles.heading: Election of members of Ad Hoc Committee and its bureau (1) Candidates for membership of an Ad Hoc
articles.text:
Committee are nominated by the Bureau
of the Senate and approved en bloc by the
Plenary Assembly by an absolute
majority of the votes of Senators present
at the sitting.
(2) From among the approved members of
the Ad Hoc Committee, the Bureau of the
Senate proposes to the Plenary Assembly
the members of the bureau of the Ad Hoc
Committee, consisting of a chairperson
and a vice chairperson, for approval by
the Plenary Assembly, each approved
separately by an absolute majority of the
votes of Senators present at the sitting.
(3) Where the Plenary Assembly does not
51
approve the members of an Ad Hoc
Committee or either or both members of
its bureau, the Bureau of the Senate
submits new nominations of candidates
for approval at the next plenary sitting.
Section 5: Committee

articles.heading: Members and bureau of the Committee (1) The Committee comprises at least five Senators, nominated by the Bureau of the
articles.text:
Senate for approval by the Plenary
Assembly.
(2) The Committee has a bureau comprising
a chairperson and a vice chairperson who
are elected by the Plenary Assembly in
accordance with the provisions of Article
21 of this Organic Law.

articles.heading: Concurrent membership of the Committee and of the Standing Committee Senators who are members of the Committee
articles.text:
retain their membership of the Standing
Committees. However, the chairperson and
the vice chairperson of the Committee may
not hold membership of the bureau of any
Standing Committee.
52

articles.heading: Term of office and procedures for replacement of members of the bureau of the Committee (1) Members of the bureau of the Committee
articles.text:
hold office for a renewable term of two
and a half years.
(2) Either or both members of the bureau of
the Committee may be replaced upon
resignation, or at the written request of
two-thirds of the members of the
Committee. A letter of resignation or
requesting the replacement is submitted
to the President of the Senate.
(3) At the request of two-thirds of the
members of the Committee, the President
of the Senate forthwith refers the matter
to the Conference of Chairpersons for
consideration. In such a case, any person
personally concerned by the matter is
ordered to withdraw.
(4) The report of the Conference of
Chairpersons on the consideration of a
matter regarding the replacement of
either or both members of the bureau of
the Committee is presented, for decision,
to the Plenary Assembly within seven
days of its submission to the Plenary
Assembly.
53
(5) Where either or both members of the
bureau of the Committee resign, or where
the Plenary Assembly decides their
replacement, the replacement is made
according to the procedures provided for
under Article 21 of this Organic Law
within 15 days of the date on which the
resignation is delivered to the President
of the Senate or of the Plenary
Assembly’s decision for their
replacement.
Section 6: Office of the Clerk

articles.heading: Organisation of Office of the Clerk (1) The Office of the Clerk comprises the services of the Senate that support the
articles.text:
Senate in the discharge of its
responsibilities.
(2) All services of the Senate fall under the
authority of the Clerk. Their functioning
is monitored by the Bureau of the Senate.

articles.heading: Establishment of organisational structure of the Senate A Presidential Order establishes the
articles.text:
organisational structure of the Senate.
54

articles.heading: Appointment of Clerk and of Deputy Clerk
Recruitment, salary and benefits of staff members placed under the authority of Office of the Clerk
articles.text:
(1) Subject to the provisions of Article 29
of this Organic Law, the staff members
placed under the authority of the Office
of the Clerk is recruited in accordance
with the relevant legislation.
(2) The salary and benefits granted to the
staff members of the Senate are
determined in accordance with the
relevant legislation.
CHAPTER III: FUNCTIONING OF THE
ORGANS OF THE SENATE
Section One: Responsibilities and
functioning of Plenary Assembly
Subsection One: Responsibilities of
Plenary Assembly
55

articles.heading: Responsibilities of Plenary Assembly (1) The Plenary Assembly is the supreme decision-making organ of the Senate
articles.text:
(2) The Plenary Assembly has the following
responsibilities:
(a) to elect members of the bureaus of
the Standing Committees;
(b) to approve the members of the
Committee and elect its bureau;
(c) to adopt the programme of business
for the ordinary session and
extraordinary session;
(d) to consider and decide on the items
on the order of business of the
plenary sitting;
(e) to decide on a motion by a Senator to
alter the order of business;
(f) to decide on the adjournment of the
plenary sitting;
(g) to determine the necessity of and
vote on Draft Laws or Private
Member’s Bills;
56
(h) to decide the referral of a Draft Law
or a Private Member’s Bill to the
Conference of Chairpersons for
consideration;
(i) to adopt a resolution on reports of
Standing Committees and those of
the Committee;
(j) to approve the appointment of
officials;
(k) to adopt Hansard reports of plenary
sittings;
(l) to rule on the publication of the
Hansard reports and the minutes of
proceedings of plenary sittings held
in camera;
(m) to decide on the establishment of an
Ad Hoc Committee, define its
mandate and elect its members and
office-bearers;
(n) to decide on the establishment of a
Committee of Inquiry, define its
mandate and elect its members and
office-bearers;
(o) to approve the resolutions of the
Conference of Chairpersons;
57
(p) to confer functions on other organs
of the Senate, where necessary;
(q) to approve the establishment of a
network or forum of Senators and
dissolve it, where necessary;
(r) to take action against a Senator
having committed a disciplinary
breach;
(s) to decide on a matter in respect of
which the Conference of
Chairpersons has failed to reach
agreement;
(t) to elect representatives of Parliament
to international organisations;
(u) to determine the commencement and
end of the official leave period for
Senators;
(v) to confirm the definitive vacancy in
the office of President, that of one or
both of Vice Presidents, or of all
members of the Bureau of the
Senate;
(w) to rule on any matter which does not
fall within the remit of any organ of
the Senate.
58
Subsection 2: Functioning of the Plenary
Assembly

articles.heading: Ordinary sessions of the Senate (1) The Senate holds three ordinary sessions, with a duration of two months each
articles.text:
(a) the first session which commences on
05 October and concludes on 04
December;
(b) the second session which commences
on 05 February and concludes on 04
April;
(c) the third session which commences
on 05 June and concludes on 04
August.
(2) Where the first or last day of a session
falls on a non-working day, the
commencement or conclusion of the
session is postponed until the next
working day.
(3) Between ordinary sessions, the Standing
Committee continues to conduct its
business and undertake public outreach
visits.
59

articles.heading: Convening of ordinary session Senators are convened to an ordinary session by the President of the Senate at least 15 days
articles.text:
before the plenary sitting, by written notice
delivered or communicated to Senators by
electronic means, through the media, or by
any other means of communication. Such a
written notice includes the draft programme
of business to be transacted during the
session. It is communicated to the President
of the Republic, the Speaker of the Chamber
of Deputies and the Prime Minister.

articles.heading: Programme of business for the ordinary session At the first sitting of the ordinary session, the
articles.text:
Plenary Assembly adopts the programme of
business for the entire session.

articles.heading: Presenting to the Plenary Assembly account of business carried out during ordinary session At the conclusion of the ordinary session, the
articles.text:
President of the Senate presents to the
60
Plenary Assembly a brief account of the
business carried out by the Senate during the
session.

articles.heading: Convening of extraordinary session (1) The President of the Senate may, after consultation with the other members of
articles.text:
the Bureau of the Senate, convene the
Plenary Assembly for an extraordinary
session, or do so at the request of the
President of the Republic or of onequarter of the Senators.
(2) An extraordinary session considers only
the matters for which it has been
convened and which have been
communicated to Senators prior to the
commencement of the session.
(3) An extraordinary session may not exceed
15 days.

articles.heading: Procedures for convening extraordinary session (1) Senators are convened to an extraordinary session by the President of
articles.text:
the Senate by written notice, which is
delivered or communicated to them by
electronic means, through the media, or
61
by any other means of communication.
(2) The written notice convening Senators to
an extraordinary session includes the
draft programme of business to be
transacted during the session, and a copy
of the notice is transmitted to the
President of the Republic and the Prime
Minister.
(3) The Plenary Assembly debates only on
the items on the programme of business
for the extraordinary session and decides
thereon.

articles.heading: Official leave period for Senators (1) Subject to the provisions of Article 33 of this Organic Law, all Senators are
articles.text:
entitled, each year, to an official leave
period of 30 calendar days, to be taken
during the interval between the third
ordinary session and the first session.
(2) The Plenary Assembly has exclusive
authority to determine the
commencement and conclusion of such
official leave period.
62
(3) The official leave may be taken in one
continuous period or in such separate
periods as determined by the Plenary
Assembly.
(4) Where there are grounds for noncompliance with the provisions of
Paragraph (1) of this Article, the Plenary
Assembly may determine another period
for the commencement of the official
leave.
(5) An extraordinary session may, where
necessary, be convened during the
official leave period.
Subsection 3: Holding of plenary sitting

articles.heading: Hours of business of the Plenary Assembly (1) The business of the Plenary Assembly commences at 3.00 p.m. and concludes
articles.text:
at 6.00 p.m. However, the Bureau of the
Senate may vary the time of
commencement of the business of the
Plenary Assembly, provided that the
duration of the business does not exceed
three hours.
(2) Hours of conclusion of the business of
63
the plenary sitting may, at the request of
the presiding officer for the plenary
sitting, be varied with the approval of the
Senators present at the sitting, by
consensus. Where consensus is not
reached, the variation is determined by
the vote of an absolute majority of the
votes of Senators present at the sitting.
(3) However, where the time for conclusion
of business is reached while the person
granted the floor still has it, the presiding
officer for the sitting waits until he or she
concludes before requesting an
extension.

articles.heading: Venue of the plenary sitting (1) The plenary sitting of the Senate is held in the Senate building in the Capital City
articles.text:
of the Republic of Rwanda, except in
circumstances of force majeure
confirmed by the Supreme Court at the
request of the President of the Senate.
Where the Supreme Court is itself unable
to sit, the President of the Republic, by
decree-law, determines the venue of the
sitting.
(2) The Senate makes public the decision
64
referred to in Paragraph (1) of this Article
by electronic means, through the media,
or by any other means of communication.

articles.heading: Holding and quorum of the plenary sitting (1) For the plenary sitting to be validly held, it must be held in the building designated
articles.text:
for that purpose, convened upon notice,
on the basis of an order of business, held
during a session, and attended by at least
three-fifths of the Senators.
(2) The plenary sitting may be held only if
at least two members of the Bureau of
the Senate are present.
(3) At each plenary sitting, every Senator
records his or her attendance by signing
against his or her name on the attendance
list or by electronic means indicating
attendance at the sitting. Prior to the
commencement of the plenary sitting,
the presiding officer for the sitting
announces the number of Senators
present at the sitting.
65
(4) Except in the event of force majeure
referred to in Article 41 of this Organic
Law, any resolution of the plenary sitting
held in contravention of the provisions
of Paragraph (1) of this Article is null
and void.

articles.heading: Principle of public access to plenary sittings (1) The plenary sittings are open to the public
articles.text:
(2) However, at the request of the President
of the Republic, the President of the
Senate, the Prime Minister, or of onequarter of the Senators, the Plenary
Assembly may sit in camera, provided
that such request is approved by an
absolute majority of the votes of the
Senators present at the sitting.
(3) A decision to hold a plenary sitting in
camera is made public by electronic
means, through the media, or by any
other means of communication.
66

articles.heading: Arrangement of seats in the plenary chamber (1) Senators are assigned permanent seats in the plenary chamber in alphabetical
articles.text:
order of their names as they appear on
the national identity card.
(2) However, the Bureau of the Senate may,
on grounds of disability or any other
cause, approve an exemption from the
provisions of Paragraph (1) of this
Article. Such a decision is
communicated to all Senators.
(3) Seats are also reserved for members of
the Bureau of the Senate, representatives
of the Government, and other persons
participating in the business of the
Plenary Assembly.

articles.heading: Weekly programme of business of the Plenary Assembly (1) The draft weekly programme of business
articles.text:
of the Plenary Assembly is prepared by
the Clerk on the basis of the items
included in the programme of business
for the session and submitted to the
Bureau of the Senate for approval.
67
(2) The order of business of the Plenary
Assembly is transmitted to the Senators at
least two days before the items listed
thereon are considered in the plenary
sitting, except in cases of urgency. Such
an order of business is made public by
electronic means, through the media, or
by any other means of communication.

articles.heading: Time limit for transmission to Senators of document due for consideration at plenary sitting
articles.text:
A document containing items to be
considered by the Plenary Assembly is
submitted to the Senators at least seven days
in advance of their consideration by the
Plenary Assembly. The time limit provided
for under this Article is waived in the case of
a request for expedited procedure in respect
of an item to be considered.

articles.heading: Suspension of plenary sitting (1) When the quorum for the plenary sitting is not attained, the presiding officer for
articles.text:
the plenary sitting declares that the sitting
cannot proceed and suspends it.
68
(2) Where any other justifiable cause arises
for the suspension of a sitting already in
progress, the presiding officer for the
plenary sitting informs the Plenary
Assembly thereof for decision.
(3) Where a justifiable cause arises for the
suspension of a sitting already scheduled,
the President of the Senate informs the
Senators thereof by means of a written
notice transmitted by electronic means,
through the media, or by any other means
of communication.
Subsection 4: Procedures for presiding
over plenary sitting

articles.heading: Presiding over plenary sitting (1) The presiding officer for the plenary sitting coordinates the exchange of views,
articles.text:
announces the stage reached in the debate
on an item under consideration, and calls
to order those who go off the topic.
(2) The presiding officer for the plenary
sitting calls to order any person who
exerts influence on the Plenary Assembly
69
to secure acceptance or rejection of a
particular view, or who, by any means
whatsoever, attempts to obstruct the
Plenary Assembly in arriving at a
decision.
(3) The presiding officer for the plenary
sitting, at all times, refrains from taking
sides in the course of debates.

articles.heading: Procedures for presiding over plenary sitting when the matter under consideration concerns a member of the
articles.text:
Bureau
(1) Where the plenary sitting deliberates on
a matter concerning the President of the
Senate, the sitting is presided over by the
Vice President of the Senate, in
accordance with the provisions of this
Organic Law. In such a case, the
President of the Senate takes the seat
reserved for him or her in his or her
capacity as a Senator.
(2) Where the plenary sitting deliberates on
a matter concerning a Vice President of
the Senate, such a Vice President takes
the seat reserved for him or her in his or
her capacity as a Senator.
70

articles.heading: Procedures for presiding over the plenary sitting considering a matter concerning members of the Bureau of the
articles.text:
Senate
(1) The plenary sitting convened to
deliberate on a matter concerning the
members of the Bureau of the Senate is
convened by the President of the Senate
and presided over by the Senator with the
longest continuous service in the Senate
or, where two or more Senators have the
same length of continuous service, by the
eldest among them. Where the President
of the Senate fails to summon the sitting,
it is convened and presided over by the
Senator with the longest continuous
service in the Senate or, if there are two
or more such Senators with equal length
of service, by the eldest among them.
(2) Where the plenary sitting deliberates on a
matter concerning the members of the
Bureau of the Senate, they take the seats
reserved for them in their respective
capacities as Senators.

articles.heading: Motion to amend the order of business (1) A Senator who has a matter to raise which is of urgent importance with a direct or
articles.text:
71
indirect impact on national public interest
may move to amend the order of business
of the plenary sitting.
(2) The motion is presented in writing to the
President of the Senate not less than five
hours before the commencement of the
plenary sitting. This time limit may be
waived where the plenary sitting is
convened under circumstances of
urgency.
(3) The Senator moving to amend the order
of business of the plenary sitting is
granted the floor before the consideration
of the items on the order of business
begins and is permitted to speak for not
more than ten minutes.
(4) A decision on the relevance of the matter
is made by an absolute majority of the
votes of the Senators present at the
plenary sitting.
(5) Where the Plenary Assembly determines
that the matter is of urgent importance, it
forthwith proceeds to its consideration.
Where it is not of urgent importance, it is
resolved to consider it later or refer it to
the competent Standing Committee for
72
prior consideration.

articles.heading: Request for inclusion on the first, second or third list (1) A Senator wishing to speak in the plenary
articles.text:
sitting registers on the first, second or
third list.
(2) Registration on the first list is effected by
written notice submitted to the President
of the Senate no later than five hours
before the holding of the plenary sitting.
The first list is transmitted to Senators
prior to the commencement of the plenary
sitting and indicates the order in which
Senators are to be called to speak, as well
as the item on the order of business on
which each Senator intends to intervene.
The speaking time allotted to a Senator
registered on the first list cannot exceed a
maximum of 15 minutes.
(3) Registration on the second list is effected
through the electronic system used for
requesting the floor or for voting and
opens after the sponsor of the Draft Law
or Private Member’s Bill, or the person
having presented the matter under
73
consideration, has replied to Senators
registered on the first list. The second list
is communicated to the Plenary
Assembly before the floor is granted to
the Senators registered thereon. Each
Senator registered on the second list is
allotted a speaking time of a maximum of
five minutes.
(4) The third and final list is opened after
replies have been given to the questions
posed by Senators registered on the
second list. Senators register through the
electronic system used for requesting the
floor or for voting. The third list is
communicated to the Plenary Assembly
prior to the granting of the floor to the
Senators registered thereon. Each Senator
registered on the third list is allotted a
speaking time of a maximum of five
minutes.
(5) Where, during registration on the second
or third list, the electronic system used for
requesting the floor or for voting fails to
function properly, a Senator requesting
the floor indicates it by show of hands, or
by any other means where a show of
hands is not feasible, prior to the
allocation of the floor by the presiding
officer for the sitting.
74

articles.heading: Being granted the floor in the plenary sitting (1) A Senator who requests the floor under the conditions provided for under this
articles.text:
Organic Law is granted the floor.
(2) A Senator takes the floor after it has been
granted by the presiding officer for the
plenary sitting, in accordance with the
announced list.
(3) The Prime Minister, a Minister, a
Minister of State, or any other member of
the Government, the chairperson or vice
chairperson of the Committee having
considered an item, a Senator being
personally concerned by the matter, the
sponsor of a Draft Law or Private
Member’s Bill and any person having
presented to the Plenary Assembly a
report of an organ provided for under the
Constitution of the Republic of Rwanda,
are granted the floor whenever they so
request.
(4) Where necessary, the presiding officer for
the plenary sitting, at the conclusion of
each list, summarizes the principal
observations made during the debate.
(5) A Senator who is a member of the
75
Committee having presented a report is
granted the floor whenever he or she so
requests to supplement the interventions
by the bureau of the Committee.

articles.heading: Speaking place for a person granted the floor in the plenary sitting (1) A person granted the floor during the
articles.text:
plenary sitting whose name appears on
the first list speaks, where practicable,
from the place designated for that
purpose.
(2) A person granted the floor during the
plenary sitting and whose name appears
on the second or third list, or who is
granted the floor to present a motion,
speaks from his or her seat.

articles.heading: Seeking leave to move a motion (1) A Senator may seek leave to move a motion and speak for not more than three
articles.text:
minutes in doing so to:
(a) raise a point of order;
(b) make a personal statement;
76
(c) seek a reply to his or her unanswered
question;
(d) move the closure of debate;
(e) to seek a brief suspension of the
plenary sitting;
(f) to seek the adjournment of the
business of the plenary sitting.
(2) The motions referred to in Paragraph
(1)(d) (e)(f) of this Article are subject to
approval by the Plenary Assembly by
consensus or, failing that, by a majority of
at least three-fifths of the Senators
present at the sitting.
(3) No motion may be moved:
(a) while a Senator who has been granted
the floor is still speaking;
(b) once the putting to the vote has
commenced.
(4) A person seeking leave to move a motion
indicates it in the manner prescribed for
requesting the floor in the plenary sitting
or by placing the palm of one hand held
77
horizontally over the fingers of the other,
raised vertically. If, by reason of
disability or any other cause, he or she is
unable to do so, he or she signifies it in
any other manner convenient for him or
her.

articles.heading: Conduct required of a person having the floor in the plenary sitting (1) A person granted the floor in the plenary
articles.text:
sitting addresses no one other than the
presiding officer for the plenary sitting.
(2) If a person having the floor goes off the
topic or repeats arguments already made,
the presiding officer for the plenary
sitting must interrupt him or her and has
the sole authority to bring him or her back
to the items under discussion.
(3) If the person who has the floor is called to
order twice but continues to go off the
topic or repeat arguments already made,
the presiding officer withdraws the floor
from him or her for the remainder of the
debate on the matter.
78

articles.heading: Prohibitions during the plenary sitting (1) During the plenary sitting, the use of insulting, offensive or provocative
articles.text:
language, the utterance of disruptive
shouts, any conduct disrupting the order,
or obstruction of another person’s
intervention are prohibited.
(2) The interruption of a person who has the
floor is prohibited, except by the
presiding officer for the plenary sitting
and only for the purpose of raising a point
of order.

articles.heading: Closure of debate (1) The presiding officer for the plenary sitting indicates the stage reached in the
articles.text:
debate and declares the debate closed
once all those having requested the floor
have completed their intervention.
(2) The presiding officer for the plenary
sitting may also propose the closure of
debate on an item under consideration
when, in his or her opinion, the item has
been sufficiently discussed by the
Plenary Assembly, subject to approval by
the Plenary Assembly by consensus or,
failing that, by an absolute majority of
79
the votes of the Senators present at the
sitting.
Subsection 5: Decision-making

articles.heading: Procedures for decisionmaking (1) The Plenary Assembly makes its decisions by consensus or by a vote
articles.text:
(2) Subject to the provisions of the
Constitution of the Republic of Rwanda
and of this Organic Law relating to
decision-making in the plenary sitting,
when the Plenary Assembly has to
decide on a matter other than legislation,
the presiding officer for the plenary
sitting inquires whether any Senator
objects to the decision proposed by him
or her or by another Senator. If no
objection is raised, the decision is
deemed taken by consensus. If an
objection is raised, the matter is put to a
vote, to be conducted by electronic
means, by show of hands, or by any
other method where a show of hands is
impracticable.
80

articles.heading: Methods of voting (1) Voting is conducted by any of the following methods
articles.text:
(a) electronic means;
(b) show of hands;
(c) roll call;
(d) written ballot.
(2) Before proceeding to a vote, the presiding
officer for the plenary sitting announces
the number of Senators present at the
sitting in compliance with the procedures
provided for under Article 42 of this
Organic Law.
(3) Where the Plenary Assembly has to make
a decision concerning an individual,
voting is by written ballot or by electronic
means.
(4) Subject to the provisions of the
Constitution of the Republic of Rwanda
and of this Organic Law relating to the
methods of voting in the plenary sitting,
decisions of the plenary sitting are made
by an absolute majority of the votes of the
Senators present at the sitting.
81

articles.heading: Retaking of vote (1) Where irregularities occur during a vote, the vote is retaken immediately after the
articles.text:
declaration of the voting results, at the
request of the presiding officer for the
plenary sitting or of at least one Senator,
subject to approval by the Plenary
Assembly.
(2) Without prejudice to the provisions of

articles.heading: Voting by written ballot (1) Where a vote takes place by secret ballot, the Clerk provides each Senator present
articles.text:
with a ballot paper bearing only the
official stamp of the Senate and the
signature of the presiding officer for the
plenary sitting.
(2) Upon casting a vote, each Senator folds
the ballot paper and places it in the
receptacle designated for that purpose.
82
(3) The counting of the ballot papers used
and of the votes takes place forthwith,
before the Senators, and is conducted by
a representative of the Bureau of the
Senate, assisted by the Clerk and by two
Senators jointly designated by the
presiding officer for the plenary sitting
and the Clerk.
(4) Ballot papers left blank and any ballot
paper bearing a mark other than that
provided for under Paragraph (1) of this
Article are treated as invalid.
(5) Any ballot papers bearing an expression
other than that required by the question
put to the vote are treated as invalid.

articles.heading: Voting procedures guide (1) Matters related to the election of members of the bureaus of the Standing
articles.text:
Committees and of the bureau of the
Committee which are not provided for
under this Organic Law are set out in
detail in the voting procedures guide of
the Bureau of the Senate.
(2) The voting procedures guide of the
Bureau of the Senate also determines
83
matters related to other elections which
may be conducted by written ballot.

articles.heading: Tearing up ballot papers used for voting At the close of a vote conducted by written ballot, the ballot papers used for voting are
articles.text: torn up before the Plenary Assembly.

articles.heading: Announcement of order of business for the next plenary sitting Upon completion of the consideration of all
articles.text:
items on the order of business by the plenary
sitting, the presiding officer therefor
announces the date, time and order of
business for the next sitting.

articles.heading: Minutes and Hansard report of plenary sitting (1) Minutes and Hansard report are drawn up for each plenary sitting. The reading of
articles.text:
the minutes and of the Hansard report
does not take place in the plenary sitting.
(2) The minutes comprise a summary record
84
of the deliberations of the plenary sitting.
(3) All oral interventions made during the
plenary sitting are audio-recorded, using
appropriate equipment and are
transcribed in the Hansard report. The
Hansard report contains a word-for-word
record of the debates and is made
available within 30 days of the plenary
sitting concerned and submitted to the
Senators.
(4) Where the plenary sitting of the Senate is
held in camera, the minutes and Hansard
report are drawn up and kept by the Clerk.
The Senate decides, by resolution, on
their publication and, where appropriate,
on the commencement of their use.

articles.heading: Adoption, signing and publication of minutes and Hansard report (1) The minutes are adopted by the Bureau of
articles.text:
the Senate, while the Hansard report is
adopted by the Plenary Assembly.
85
(2) The Plenary Assembly adopts Hansard
reports of an ordinary session no later
than the first month of the ordinary
session immediately following that
during which the sittings to which those
reports relate were held.
(3) The adoption of the Hansard reports of an
extraordinary session takes place during
the final week of the immediately
following ordinary session.
(4) A Senator wishing to propose a correction
to the Hansard report submits the
proposed correction in writing to the
President of the Senate not less than 48
hours before the next plenary sitting and
gives a copy thereof to all Senators.
(5) The adopted minutes are jointly signed by
the presiding officer for the sitting and the
Clerk.
(6) The Hansard report adopted by the
Plenary Assembly is jointly signed by the
presiding officer for the sitting concerned
and the Clerk. Where the presiding
officer having presided over that sitting is
no longer a Senator, the Hansard report is
jointly signed by the presiding officer for
86
the sitting at which it is adopted and the
Clerk.
(7) The adopted minutes and Hansard reports
are published on the website of
Parliament and deposited in the library of
the Senate.

articles.heading: Address by a State guest to Senators (1) A State guest may address the Senators
articles.text:
The sitting at which such address is
delivered is convened by the President of
the Senate.
(2) The Bureau of the Senate may designate
a Senator to deliver a brief address, by
way of a vote of thanks, to a State guest
following his or her address to the
Senators.
Section 2: Responsibilities and functioning
of the Conference of Chairpersons

articles.heading: Responsibilities of the Conference of Chairpersons (1) The Conference of Chairpersons is responsible for
articles.text:
87
(a) to adopt the draft programme of
business for the ordinary session;
(b) to make resolutions relating to the
activities of Senators, of the Plenary
Assembly, or of the Standing
Committees;
(c) to consider Draft Laws or Private
Member’s Bills if so decided by the
Plenary Assembly;
(d) to provide opinions on the draft
organisational structure of the Senate;
(e) to perform any other function as may
be assigned by the Plenary Assembly.
(2) The Conference of Chairpersons
determines which of its resolutions are
to be submitted to the Plenary
Assembly.

articles.heading: Functioning of and decisionmaking by the Conference of Chairpersons (1) The Conference of Chairpersons meets
articles.text:
once a month and whenever necessary,
and is duly constituted when at least
three-fifths of its members are present. It
88
is convened and chaired by the President
of the Senate.
(2) A member of the bureau of the
Committee may attend the meeting of the
Conference of Chairpersons. He or she
takes the floor therein, but without voting
rights.
(3) The Conference of Chairpersons makes
decisions by consensus or, failing that,
the item under debate is referred to the
Plenary Assembly for decision.
(4) When considering a draft law or a Private
Member’s Bill, the Conference of
Chairpersons complies with the
provisions of this Organic Law relating to
the functioning of the Standing
Committees in the consideration of draft
laws or Private Member’s Bills.

articles.heading: Report of the meeting of the Conference of Chairpersons (1) The report of the meeting of the
articles.text:
Conference of Chairpersons is
transmitted to the Senators.
(2) A Senator may, where necessary and
upon written request, propose that such a
report be debated in the plenary sitting.
89
Section 3: Responsibilities and functioning
of the Bureau of the Senate
Subsection One: Responsibilities of the
Bureau of the Senate and of its members

articles.heading: Responsibilities of the Bureau of the Senate The Bureau of the Senate has the following responsibilities
articles.text:
(a) to direct the business of the Senate;
(b) to monitor working relations between
the Senate and other organs;
(c) to comply with and implement the
decisions of the Plenary Assembly;
(d) to determine items for inclusion on the
agenda of the meeting of the
Conference of Chairpersons;
(e) to submit to the Conference of
Chairpersons the draft programme of
business for the ordinary session of the
Plenary Assembly;
(f) to prepare and adopt the draft
programme of business for the
extraordinary session;
90
(g) to adopt the minutes of the plenary
sitting;
(h) to monitor the preparation of the
organisational structure of the Senate
and submit it to the Conference of
Chairpersons for opinion thereon;
(i) to monitor the recruitment, deployment,
and performance appraisal of the staff
members of the Senate;
(j) to monitor security-related matters
within the building of the Senate;
(k) to monitor the functioning of
parliamentary networks or forums;
(l) to determine which committee reports
may be transmitted to other organs or
published on the website of Parliament;
(m) to decide on the establishment of a
friendship group, determine its
mandate, and monitor its functioning;
(n) to receive and assess the declarations of
assets submitted by the Ombudsman,
91
Deputy Ombudsmen, and other staff
members of the Office of the
Ombudsman who are required to
declare their assets;
(o) to adopt a document outlining
procedures for the conduct of the
election of members of the bureaus of
Standing Committees and of the
Committee, and of representatives of
the Senate to inter-parliamentary
organisations, and to preside over such
election;
(p) to approve the admission of a former
Head of State as a Senator;
(q) to resolve matters likely to hinder the
functioning of the Senate that are not
covered by this Organic Law, and
perform any other duties within the
remit of the Senate not assigned to any
other service;
(r) to perform such other duties as may be
assigned by the Plenary Assembly or
the Conference of Chairpersons.
92

articles.heading: Responsibilities of the President of the Senate The President of the Senate – (a) monitors and coordinates activities of
Responsibilities of the Vice President in charge of Parliamentary Affairs The Vice President in charge of
articles.text:
Parliamentary Affairs –
(a) assists the President of the Senate and
replaces him or her during his or her
absence;
(b) replaces the Vice President in charge
of Administration and Finance during
his or her absence;
95
(c) monitors activities relating to the
consideration of Draft Laws or
Private Member’s Bills;
(d) monitors the manner in which the
Senate monitors the application of the
fundamental principles whenever it
discharges its responsibilities and
exercises its powers;
(e) monitors the activities related to the
monitoring of the functioning of
political organisations;
(f) monitors activities related to the
approval of the appointment of
officials;
(g) monitors and coordinates the
activities of Standing Committees;
(h) monitors activities related to the
exercise of oversight of Government
activities;
(i) monitors matters related to working
relations between the Senate and
other local and foreign entities;
(j) monitors the activities of Senators
related to public outreach visits;
96
(k) monitors activities of networks or
forums or a national chapter of an
international network and forum and
those of friendship groups;
(l) develops the guide of the Bureau of
the Senate on the voting procedures
for members of the bureaus of
Standing Committees and of the
Committee, and of representatives of
the Senate to inter-parliamentary
organisations;
(m) performs any such other duties as
may be assigned to him or her by the
Bureau the Senate.

articles.heading: Responsibilities of the Vice President in charge of Administration and Finance The Vice President in charge of
articles.text:
Administration and Finance –
(a) assists the President of the Senate in
the discharge of his or her duties;
(b) replaces the President of the Senate in
case of the concurrent absence of the
97
latter and of the Vice President in
charge of Parliamentary Affairs;
(c) replaces the Vice President in charge
of Parliamentary Affairs in case of his
or her absence;
(d) monitors, from financial and
administrative perspectives, facilities
which support the Senators in the
discharge of their responsibilities;
(e) monitors the activities related to
financial management and
administration;
(f) monitors the activities related to the
preparation, execution and
management of the budget of the
Senate;
(g) monitors matters related to the
recruitment of the staff members of
the Senate and their performance
appraisal;
(h) monitors the performance of the
Senate’s internal auditor and of the
audit committee in the Senate;
(i) performs any such other duties as
98
may be assigned to him or her by the
Bureau of the Senate.
Subsection 2: Functioning of the Bureau of
the Senate

articles.heading: Holding of the meeting of the Bureau of the Senate and procedures for decision-making (1) Subject to the provisions of Article 39 of
articles.text:
this Organic Law, the Bureau of the
Senate meets once a week and whenever
necessary.
(2) Decisions of the Bureau of the Senate are
made by consensus among its members.
Where consensus is not reached, the item
under discussion is, at the request of the
President or a Vice President, referred to
the Conference of Chairpersons for
decision.
(3) Where consensus is not reached by the
Conference of Chairpersons, the item
under discussion is referred to the Plenary
Assembly for decision.
(4) The meeting of the Bureau of the Senate
is the subject of a report jointly signed by
the chair of the meeting and the Clerk.
99

articles.heading: Receipt and verification of declaration of assets of members of the Office of the Ombudsman
articles.text:
(1) Written declarations of assets by the
Ombudsman, Deputy Ombudsmen and
other staff members of the Office of the
Ombudsman required to declare their
assets are submitted to the Bureau of the
Senate in accordance with the relevant
legislation.
(2) In verifying the declarations of the
Ombudsman, Deputy Ombudsmen and
other staff members of the Office of the
Ombudsman required to declare their
assets, the Bureau of the Senate assesses
the accuracy of the declarations
submitted and the sources of the assets
declared.
(3) The Bureau of the Senate may seek the
assistance of other competent public
organs in inquiring into matters relating
to the declarations of assets of the
Ombudsman, Deputy Ombudsmen and
other staff members of the Office of the
Ombudsman required to declare their
assets.
Subsection 3: Vacancy in the office and
replacement of member of the Bureau of
the Senate
100

articles.heading: Grounds for vacancy in the office of member of the Bureau of the Senate (1) A member of the Bureau of the Senate
articles.text:
vacates such an office upon resigning or
upon ceasing to be a Senator.
(2) The Plenary Assembly of the Senate may
remove from office a member, two
members, or all members of the Bureau
of the Senate. A decision to remove a
Senator from membership of the Bureau
of the Senate is made by an absolute
majority of the votes of those present at
the plenary sitting.

articles.heading: Written notice of resignation of a member of the Bureau of the Senate (1) When the President of the Senate resigns
articles.text:
from that capacity, he or she tenders his or
her resignation in writing to the members
of the Plenary Assembly and informs the
President of the Republic thereof.
(2) When the Vice President resigns from that
capacity, he or she tenders his or her
resignation in writing to the President of the
Senate and informs the President of the
Republic and the Senators thereof.
101
(3) When all the members of the Bureau of the
Senate resign from their respective
capacities, each member tenders his or her
resignation in writing to the members of the
Plenary Assembly and informs the
President of the Republic thereof.

articles.heading: Convening of the sitting to establish the vacancy in the office of a member of the Bureau of the Senate
articles.text:
(1) Where a member of the Bureau of the
Senate vacates his or her office for a
reason other than a decision of the
Plenary Assembly or death, the Plenary
Assembly is convened for the purpose of
establishing that no Senator holds that
office. The decision is made by consensus
among the Senators present at the sitting
or, failing that, by an absolute majority of
the votes of the Senators present at the
sitting.
(2) Where the President of the Senate vacates
his or her office, the Vice President in
charge of Parliamentary Affairs convenes
and presides over the plenary sitting held
for the purpose of establishing that no
Senator holds that office.
102
(3) Where a Vice President vacates his or her
office, the plenary sitting held for the
purpose of establishing that no Senator
holds that office is convened and presided
over by the President of the Senate.
(4) Where two members of the Bureau of the
Senate vacate their respective offices, the
plenary sitting held for the purpose of
establishing that no Senators hold those
offices is convened and presided over by
the remaining member of the Bureau of
the Senate, assisted by the eldest Senator
among those Senators with the longest
continuous service in the Senate.
(5) Where all the members of the Bureau of
the Senate vacate their respective offices,
the plenary sitting held for the purpose of
establishing that no Senators hold those
offices is convened and presided over by
the eldest Senator among those Senators
with the longest continuous service in the
Senate, acting on his or her own motion
or at the written request of at least onethird of the Senators. He or she is assisted
by the youngest Senator.
103

articles.heading: Notification of the vacancy in office of a member of the Bureau of the Senate (1) Where the Plenary Assembly establishes
articles.text:
that an office of a member of the Bureau
of the Senate is not held by a Senator, the
person having convened the plenary
sitting held for the purpose of
establishing such a fact and who is
referred to in Article 80 of this Organic
Law, informs the President of the
Republic in writing thereof, with a copy
to the Speaker of the Chamber of
Deputies, the President of the Supreme
Court, the Prime Minister and all
Senators.
(2) A notification that an office of member of
the Bureau of the Senate is not held by
any Senator is effected within 24 hours of
the establishment by the Plenary
Assembly of such a fact.

articles.heading: Conduct of the Senate’s day-today business in the event of a vacancy in offices of two, or of all, members of the
articles.text:
Bureau of the Senate
(1) Where two members of the Bureau of the
Senate vacate their respective offices, the
remaining member of the Bureau
104
conducts the day-to-day business of the
Senate, except for presiding over
meetings of the Conference of
Chairpersons or over the plenary sitting.
(2) Where all the members of the Bureau of
the Senate vacate their respective offices,
the eldest Senator among those Senators
with the longest continuous service in the
Senate conducts the day-to-day business
of the Senate, except for chairing
meetings of the Conference of
Chairpersons or presiding over the
plenary sitting.

articles.heading: Convening of a sitting held for the purpose of replacing a member of the Bureau of the Senate
articles.text:
(1) A sitting held for the purpose of replacing
a member of the Bureau of the Senate is
convened and presided over by the
President of the Republic within 30 days
of the date on which the Plenary
Assembly establishes the vacancy in that
office.
(2) A person elected to replace a member of
the Bureau of the Senate serves for the
remainder of that member’s term of
office.
105

articles.heading: Temporary replacement of the President of the Senate Where the President of the Senate has to
articles.text:
replace the President of the Republic in an
acting capacity or permanently vacates his or
her office or is otherwise prevented from
discharging the functions of his or her office,
he or she is temporarily replaced by the Vice
President of the Senate in charge of
Parliamentary Affairs.
Section 4: Responsibilities and functioning
of Standing Committees
Subsection One: Responsibilities of
Standing Committees

articles.heading: Responsibilities conferred upon all Standing Committees (1) Standing Committee share the following
articles.text:
responsibilities:
(a) to monitor the application of
fundamental principles;
(b) to consider Draft Laws or Private
Member’s Bills;
(c) to exercise oversight over
Government activities;
106
(d) to consider the files relating to the
approval of the appointment of
officials;
(e) to consider activity reports of State
organs submitted to Parliament;
(f) to provide opinions on the budget
framework paper;
(g) to consider petitions addressed to the
Senate by the population.
(2) The Plenary Assembly or the Bureau of
the Senate may, where necessary, assign
additional responsibilities to Standing
Committees.

articles.heading: Responsibilities of the Committee on Governance and Human Rights The Committee on Governance and Human
Responsibilities of the Committee on Foreign Affairs, National Unity and Security The Committee on Foreign Affairs, National
Responsibilities of the Committee on Economy and Finance (1) The Committee on Economy and Finance
Responsibilities of the Committee on Social Affairs, Education, Technology and Youth The Committee on Social Affairs, Education,
Responsibilities of the bureau of the Standing Committee (1) The responsibilities of the bureau of the
Holding of, and decisionmaking at, meetings of the bureau of the Standing Committee (1) Subject to the provisions of Article 38 of
articles.text:
this Organic Law, the bureau of the
Standing Committee meets once a week
and whenever necessary.
(2) Decisions of the bureau of the Standing
Committee are made by consensus
114
among its members. Where consensus is
not reached, the item under consideration
is, at the request of the chairperson or vice
chairperson of the Standing Committee,
referred to the Standing Committee for
decision.

articles.heading: Responsibilities of the Chairperson of the Standing Committee The Chairperson of the Standing Committee–
articles.text:
(a) coordinates activities of the Standing
Committee;
(b) convenes and presides over meetings
of the Standing Committee;
(c) submits activity reports of the
Standing Committee to the Bureau of
the Senate;
(d) presents activity reports of the
Standing Committee to the Plenary
Assembly; and
(e) serves as the representative and
spokesperson of the Standing
Committee.
115

articles.heading: Responsibilities of the Vice Chairperson of the Standing Committee The vice chairperson of the Standing
articles.text:
Committee –
(a) assists the Chairperson of the
Standing Committee and deputizes
for him or her in his or her absence;
(b) prepares the programme of activities
and of meetings for the Standing
Committee; and
(c) monitors the preparation of activity
reports of the Standing Committee.
Subsection 2: Functioning of the Standing
Committee

articles.heading: Convening of the meeting of the Standing Committee (1) The meeting of the Standing Committee
articles.text:
is convened in writing by its chairperson,
or, in the absence of the chairperson, by
its vice chairperson, and notice of such a
meeting is communicated to the Bureau
of the Senate and to the other Senators by
one of the means of communication or,
where practicable, by all available means
of communication.
116
(2) The written notice of the meeting
specifies the items on the agenda as
determined by the bureau of the Standing
Committee as well as the date, time and
venue of the meeting.
(3) The President of the Senate may also
convene a meeting of the Standing
Committee.
(4) The date, time and agenda of the meeting
of the Standing Committee are
announced at least 24 hours prior to the
holding of the meeting, by one of the
means of communication or, where
practicable, by all available means of
communication. However, the time limit
provided for under this Paragraph may be
varied where necessary.

articles.heading: Venue of meeting of the Standing Committee (1) The meeting of the Standing Committee is held within the
articles.text:
Parliament building.
(2) Each Standing Committee is assigned
a meeting room for the holding of its
meetings.
117
(3) Where necessary, the bureau of the
Standing Committee may, after
consultation between the bureau of
the Standing Committee and the
Bureau of the Senate, meet at a venue
other than the Parliament building or
by virtual means. In such a case, the
provisions of this Organic Law
relating to the functioning of the
Standing Committee apply.

articles.heading: Quorum and decision-making of the Standing Committee (1) The Standing Committee may validly
articles.text:
meet only if at least three-fifths of the
Senators comprising its membership
are present.
(2) The Standing Committee decides by
consensus. Failing consensus,
decisions are made by an absolute
majority of the votes of the Senators
comprising its membership who are
present at the meeting.
(3) Where the votes of the members of
the Standing Committee are equally
divided on a decision put to a vote, the
vote is taken again. Where the votes
are again equally divided,
118
consideration of the item is deferred.
Upon resumption of the meeting of
the Standing Committee on that item,
and where an absolute majority is not
reached, the Standing Committee
seeks the opinion of the Bureau of the
Senate.

articles.heading: Hours of the business of the Standing Committee (1) The business of the Standing Committee is conducted between
articles.text:
9.00 a.m. and 12.00 p.m. However,
the time of commencement of the
business may, where necessary, be
varied by decision of the chairperson
of the Standing Committee, who
gives written notice thereof to all
Senators and to the persons invited to
attend, and such variation is posted on
the website of the Senate.
(2) The time for adjournment of the meeting
of the Standing Committee may be varied
at the request of the chair of the meeting,
subject to the consensus among the
Senators comprising the membership of
the Committee who are present at the
meeting. Failing consensus, such
variation requires approval by an absolute
majority of the votes of the Senators
119
comprising its membership who are
present at the meeting. However, where
the time of adjournment is reached while
the person granted the floor still has it, the
chair of the meeting defers proposing any
variation of the adjournment until he or
she concludes his or her intervention.

articles.heading: Chairing of the meeting of the Standing Committee (1) The meeting of the Standing Committee is chaired by the
articles.text:
chairperson of the Standing
Committee, assisted by its vice
chairperson or, in the vice
chairperson’s absence, by the
youngest Senator among the
members of the Standing Committee.
(2) In the absence of the chairperson of
the Standing Committee, the vice
chairperson chairs the meeting,
assisted by the youngest Senator
among the members of the Standing
Committee.
(3) Where both of them are absent, or
have permanently ceased to hold
office and have not yet been replaced,
120
the meeting of the Standing
Committee is chaired by the oldest
Senator among those Senators with
the longest continuous service,
assisted by the youngest Senator.

articles.heading: Attending proceedings of the meeting of Standing Committee (1) The meeting of the Standing Committee is open to the public
articles.text:
However, the meeting of the Standing
Committee may, where necessary, be
held in camera, at the request of the
bureau of the Standing Committee or
of a member of the Standing
Committee, and subject to approval by
at least three-fifths of the members of
the Standing Committee present at the
meeting.
(2) Any Senator who so wishes may
attend the proceedings of the meeting
of a Standing Committee of which he
or she registered as a member and
provide opinions, but has no voting
rights.
(3) Any other person who so wishes may
attend the proceedings of the meeting
of the Standing Committee, but is not
121
granted the floor, except in the case of
special sittings at which the public
may take the floor.

articles.heading: Meeting of the Standing Committee at which any person may be granted the floor (1) A meeting of the Standing Committee
articles.text:
at which any person may be granted
the floor in relation to a Draft Law or
Private Member’s Bill, or any other
item under consideration, is decided
upon by the Standing Committee and
announced, using possible means of
communication.
(2) At the opening of the meeting, the
Chairperson of the Standing
Committee informs those present of
the procedures for taking the floor, the
maximum speaking time, and the
order of speakers to be recognized.
(3) The Standing Committee may also
receive written opinions on a Draft
Law, a Private Member’s Bill or any
other item under consideration. Any
such opinions received are submitted
to the members of the Standing
122
Committee for as long as the item to
which they relate remains under
consideration at the Standing
Committee stage.

articles.heading: Invitation to the meeting of the Standing Committee The Standing Committee may request the President of Senate to invite, on behalf of it,
articles.text:
any person whom it considers necessary for
providing it with clarifications or opinions on
an item under consideration.

articles.heading: Groups formed from among Senators who are members of the Standing Committee (1) The Standing Committee may form,
articles.text:
from among its members, groups and
assign them mandates.
(2) The Standing Committee may also
request the bureau of the Senate to
send, on a mission within the country,
a group of Senators comprising its
membership.
(3) The group sent on a mission submits
its report to the Standing Committee
having formed it.
123

articles.heading: Activity of common interest to two or more Standing Committees (1) The Bureau of the Senate may request
articles.text:
two or more Standing Committees to
consider a matter of common interest
to them.
(2) The first joint meeting of two or more
Standing Committees concerned with
an activity of common interest to
them is convened in writing after
consultation between the
chairpersons of such Standing
Committees. At that meeting, the
participants elect from among their
number a chair and a vice chair for the
meeting.
(3) In their functioning, two or more
Standing Committees holding a joint
meeting on a matter of common
interest to them comply with the
provisions of this Organic Law
relating to the functioning of the
Standing Committee.
(4) The report of two or more Standing
Committees is submitted to the
Bureau of the Senate.
124

articles.heading: Presentation of the report of the Standing Committee to the Plenary Assembly (1) The report of the Standing Committee
articles.text:
is transmitted to the President of the
Senate, with a copy to the other
members of the Bureau.
(2) The bureau of the Standing
Committee presents an oral summary
of the report at the Plenary Assembly
and responds to the questions posed.
(3) In the event of the absence of one of
the members of the bureau of the
Standing Committee, the member
present is, for that purpose, assisted
by the youngest Senator among the
members of the Standing Committee.
Subsection 3: Functioning of an Ad Hoc
Committee

articles.heading: Functioning of an Ad Hoc Committee (1) Where the Plenary Assembly establishes an Ad Hoc Committee, it
articles.text:
determines its mandate and sets the
time limit for the submission of a
report on the matter it is mandated to
125
deal with. Such a time limit may be
extended upon a written request from
the Ad Hoc Committee, specifying the
proposed duration of the extension,
subject to approval by the Plenary
Assembly.
(2) The Ad Hoc Committee may request
the summoning of any person whom it
considers capable of assisting it in
obtaining information relating to the
mandate assigned to it. It may make
video and audio recordings or take a
copy of any document it needs to
analyse.
(3) The Ad Hoc Committee is provided
with the resources necessary to enable
it to travel anywhere within the
country or abroad for the purpose of
gathering information, where
necessary.
(4) In its functioning, the Ad Hoc
Committee complies with the
provisions of this Organic Law
relating to the functioning of Standing
Committees.
126

articles.heading: Procedures for replacement of a member of an Ad Hoc Committee A member of an Ad Hoc Committee may be
articles.text:
replaced following his or her resignation or at
the request supported by two-thirds of the
members of the Ad Hoc Committee. The
written notice of resignation, or the request
for replacement of a member is transmitted to
the President of the Senate, who in turn
submits it to the Plenary Assembly for
resolution thereon.

articles.heading: Conclusion of the work of Ad Hoc Committee The work of an Ad Hoc Committee comes to an end upon the presentation of a report on its
articles.text:
findings, which findings are subject to the
adoption of a resolution by the Plenary
Assembly.
Section 5: Responsibilities and functioning
of the Committee

articles.heading: Responsibilities of the Committee The Committee has the following responsibilities
articles.text:
(a) to oversee the activities of the
127
Conference of Chairpersons, those of
the Bureau of the Senate, those of the
Standing Committees and of the
Office of the Clerk;
(b) to monitor the conduct and behaviour
of Senators, both within and outside
the Senate building, and advise them
on matters related thereto;
(c) to monitor respect for the immunity
of Senators;
(d) to provide opinions on benefits
accorded to Senators, to monitor
resolutions adopted in relation
therewith and their application.

articles.heading: Independence and decisionmaking of the Committee (1) The Committee acts independently and is
articles.text:
not subject to instructions from any
person whatsoever in respect of any
matter under its consideration.
(2) Decisions of the Committee are made by
consensus. Failing consensus, decisions
are made by an absolute majority of the
votes of the members of the Committee
present at the meeting.
128
(3) Members of the Committee act with due
regard to confidentiality in the discharge
of their functions.

articles.heading: Convening and holding of meeting of the Committee (1) The Committee has a designated room for the holding of its meetings
articles.text:
(2) The Committee meets whenever
necessary. It is convened by its
chairperson or, in the absence of the
chairperson, by the vice chairperson,
or by the President of the Senate after
consultation with the other members
of the Bureau of the Senate, or at the
request of one-third of the Senators
who are members of the Committee or
by one-fifth of the members of the
Senate.
(3) The person convening a meeting of the
Committee gives a copy of the notice
of meeting to the members of the
Bureau of the Senate.
(4) The meeting of the Committee is
attended by the Senators who are its
members and by any other person
129
invited thereto.
(5) Where a meeting of the Committee
coincides with a meeting of a Standing
Committee, a Senator who is a
member of the Committee attends the
meeting of the Committee.
(6) Where the Committee considers that,
in relation to an item it has considered,
a decision falls to be taken by another
organ, it prepares a report thereon and
submits it to the President of the
Senate, with a copy to the members of
the Bureau of the Senate.
(7) In respect of matters relating to the
functioning of the Committee not
provided for under this Organic Law,
the provisions relating to the
functioning of the Standing
Committee apply.
Section 6: Responsibilities and functioning
of the Office of the Clerk

articles.heading: Responsibilities of the Office of the Clerk The Office of the Clerk has the following responsibilities
Responsibilities of the Clerk The Clerk – (a) directs the services under the authority of the Office of the Clerk
Responsibilities of the Deputy Clerk The Deputy Clerk – (a) deputizes for the Clerk in case of the
articles.text:
Clerk’s absence;
(b) provides the Bureau of the Senate,
Standing Committees, and Senators
with advice in legal matters;
(c) attends meetings of the Bureau of the
Senate and those of the Conference of
Chairpersons;
133
(d) coordinates activities related to the
plenary sittings;
(e) monitors and coordinates, at the
technical level, the work of Standing
Committees and that of the
Committee;
(f) monitors and coordinates, at the
technical level, the work related to the
legislative drafting;
(g) monitors and coordinates the work
related to the provision of legal
advice on various documents;
(h) ensures whether any law transmitted
for publication is identical to the law
transmitted by the Senate to the
Chamber of Deputies;
(i) ensures whether any law within the
competence of the Senate published
in the of Rwanda is identical to the law
transmitted for publication;
(j) ensures whether Orders within the
competence of the Senate that are
provided for under Laws have been
134
enacted and are consistent with the
relevant legal provisions; and
(k) performs such other duties falling
under the Senate as may be assigned
by the Bureau of the Senate.
CHAPTER IV: NETWORKS OR
FORUMS OF SENATORS AND
FRIENDSHIP GROUPS
Section One: Networks or forums of
Senators

articles.heading: Establishment of a network or forum or of national chapter of an international network or forum
articles.text:
(1) The Senate may establish a network
or forum, or a national chapter of an
international network or forum of
Senators.
(2) A Senator may be a member of one or
more networks, forums, or national
chapters of international networks or
forums.
135

articles.heading: Request for and approval of the establishment of network or forum, or of national chapter of an international
articles.text:
network or forum of Senators
(1) The Plenary Assembly approves the
establishment of a network or forum,
or of a national chapter of an
international network or forum on the
basis of a request made by at least
three Senators.
(2) Senators wishing to see the
establishment of a network or forum,
or of a national chapter of an
international network or forum,
submit to the President of the Senate
a letter requesting for such an
establishment, together with a
concept paper and statutes, all of
which are placed by him or her on the
order of business of the Plenary
Assembly.
(3) Senators having sought the
establishment of a network or forum
or of a national chapter of an
international network or forum are
granted the floor during the plenary
sitting to present the reasons in
support of their request.
136

articles.heading: First meeting of a forum or network or of a national chapter of an international network or forum of
articles.text:
Senators
Following approval by the Plenary Assembly
of the establishment of a network, forum, or
national chapter of an international
parliamentary network or forum of Senators,
the first meeting of the network or forum, or
national chapter of an international network
or forum of Senators adopts its statutes and
elects its office-bearers. The statutes so
adopted and the names of the office-bearers
of the network or forum, or of a national
chapter of an international network or forum
of Senators are circulated to all Senators and
posted on the website of the Senate.

articles.heading: Statutes governing a network or forum, or national chapter of an international network or forum of
articles.text:
Senators
(1) Each network or forum, or national
chapter of an international parliamentary
network or forum of Senators has its own
governing statutes.
(2) The statutes set out, at a minimum, the
following:
137
(a) the objectives of the network or
forum or of a national chapter of an
international network or forum of
Senators;
(b) eligible members;
(c) the organs of the network or forum or
of the national chapter of an
international network or forum of
Senators;
(d) the source of, and procedures for the
management of, the property of the
network or forum or of a national
chapter of an international network or
forum of Senators;
(e) working relations between the
network or forum or national chapter
of an international network or forum
of Senators and other organs.

articles.heading: Functioning of a network or forum or of a national chapter of an international network or forum of
articles.text:
Senators
(1) In its functioning, a network or forum or
a national chapter of an international
network or forum of Senators,
endeavours to operate as:
138
(a) an innovation-oriented think tank
upon which Parliament draws;
(b) a catalyst for transformation
supporting Parliament in the
fulfilment of its responsibilities;
(c) a mobilising platform for campaigns
directed toward addressing issues of
major national concern.
(2) Where practicable, one day per week is
dedicated to activities undertaken in the
context of the network or forum or a
national chapter of an international
network or forum of Senators.

articles.heading: Activity programme and activity report of a network or forum or national chapter of an international
articles.text:
