network or forum of Senators
(1) Every quarter, and whenever necessary,
the network or forum or national chapter
of an international network or forum of
Senators, submits its activity programme
and activity report to the President of the
Senate for transmission to the Senators.
139
(2) The Plenary Assembly debates on a
report relating to an activity of a network
or forum or national chapter of an
international network or forum of
Senators, at the request of the President of
the Senate, after consultation with the
other members of the Bureau, or at the
request of a Senator.

articles.heading: Budget of a network or forum or of a national chapter of an international network or forum of Senators
articles.text:
The Senate makes provision, within its
budget, for funds intended for a network or
forum or a national chapter of an
international network of Senators.

articles.heading: Monitoring of the functioning of a network or forum or of a national chapter of an international network or
articles.text:
forum of Senators
(1) The Bureau of the Senate monitors the
functioning of a network or forum or of a
national chapter of an international
network or forum of Senators.
(2) The Plenary Assembly may, at the written
request of at least one-third of the
members of a network or forum, or of a
140
national chapter of an international
network or forum of Senators, or by a
Senator not belonging thereto, dissolve
the network or forum or the national
chapter of the international network or
forum of Senators where it has not
fulfilled its mission, where it is
incompatible with the mission or
functioning of the Senate, or where the
grounds for its establishment have ceased
to exist.
Section 2: Friendship groups

articles.heading: Establishment of friendship group (1) The Senate may establish a friendship group for the purpose of promoting
articles.text:
parliamentary diplomacy, subject to
approval by the Bureau of the Senate,
with notification thereof to all Senators.
(2) The Bureau of the Senate determines the
responsibilities of a friendship group and
appoints its members and office-bearers.
141

articles.heading: Activity programme and activity report of friendship group (1) A friendship group submits its
articles.text:
activity programme and activity
report to the President of the Senate
who, in turn, transmits them to
Senators.
(2) The Plenary Assembly debates a
report of a friendship group at the
request of the President of the Senate,
after consultation with the other
members of the Bureau, or at the
request of a Senator.
CHAPTER V: OFFICIAL MISSION OF
SENATOR WITHIN THE COUNTRY
OR ABROAD

articles.heading: Official mission of a Senator (1) A Senator may be sent on official mission within the country or abroad,
articles.text:
upon approval by the Bureau of the
Senate.
(2) Benefits granted to a Senator going
on an official mission are determined
by the relevant legislation.
142

articles.heading: Public outreach visit (1) Each Senator has the responsibility to conduct public outreach visits for the
articles.text:
purpose of identifying interventions that
contribute to bringing development to,
and challenges affecting the population.
A Senator may also identify such
interventions or challenges through
participation in meetings of decentralized
administrative entities and in other
meetings to which he or she may be
invited.
(2) A Senator may conduct public outreach
visits through a Standing Committee,
forum or network provided for under this
Organic Law, or in an individual capacity.
(3) An individual Senator is entitled to two
days per month for the purpose of
conducting public outreach visits. Such
days may accrue and be taken on a nonconsecutive basis within the same
financial year.
(4) A Senator wishing to conduct a public
outreach visit fills out the prescribed form
143
and submits it to the President of the
Senate. Such a form indicates the
proposed destination, the purpose of the
visit, and its relevance to the population
targeted for the visit and to the Senate.
The Bureau of the Senate decides on such
a request.
(5) Public outreach visits can in no way
impede the work of the Plenary Assembly
or that of the Standing Committee.

articles.heading: Collective public outreach visits by Senators (1) All Senators conduct public outreach visits collectively at least once each
articles.text:
year.
(2) The Conference of Chairpersons
prepares, for the Plenary Assembly, the
schedule of such visits and the activities
to be undertaken.

articles.heading: Official travel authorisation issued to a Senator going on domestic official mission A Senator going on a domestic official
articles.text:
mission carries an official travel
144
authorisation issued by the President of the
Senate.

articles.heading: Official travel authorization issued to a Senator going on an official mission abroad A Senator going on a foreign official mission
articles.text:
carries an official travel authorization issued
in accordance with the provisions of the
relevant legislation.

articles.heading: Submission of a report of a Senator returning from official mission A Senator returning from an official mission
articles.text:
within the country or abroad submits his or
her official mission report to the President of
the Senate within the period prescribed by the
relevant legislation. The Bureau of the Senate
determines which official mission report is
transmitted to Senators and presented to the
Plenary Assembly.
CHAPTER VI: CONDUCT OF A
SENATOR
Section One: General conduct of a Senator
145

articles.heading: Conduct of a Senator (1) A Senator must act with integrity, and in an irreproachable manner, and serve as an
articles.text:
example in complying with the
Constitution of the Republic of Rwanda
and other laws, and having due regard to
the oath of office taken prior to the
assumption of senatorial office.
(2) A Senator who fails to comply with the
provisions of Paragraph (1) of this Article
may be subject to a reminder, a warning,
a public reprimand, or exclusion from the
Senate, upon approval by a three-fifths
majority of the Senators present at the
plenary sitting.

articles.heading: Disciplinary actions applicable to Senator for act of misconduct during plenary sitting (1) Where a Senator commits an act of
articles.text:
misconduct during a plenary sitting,
any of following disciplinary actions
are applied to him or her, having
regard to the gravity of the act of
misconduct:
(a) a call to order;
146
(b) an oral warning;
(c) temporary prohibition from
occupying the seats reserved for
Senators;
(d) suspension from attending the
sitting then in progress;
(e) suspension from attending three
consecutive plenary sittings;
(f) a public reprimand.
(2) The disciplinary actions referred to in
Paragraph (1)(a)(b)(c) (d) are taken
by the presiding officer for the
plenary sitting. The disciplinary
actions referred to in Paragraph
(1)(e)(f) are taken by the Plenary
Assembly.
(3) The Senator subject to the
disciplinary action referred to in
Paragraph (1)(e) is barred from
attending three consecutive meetings
of any Standing Committee, those of
the Committee, or of the Conference
of Chairpersons if he or she is one of
their members.
147
(4) Where a Senator on whom any
disciplinary action provided for under
this Article has been imposed
commits an act of misconduct again,
his or her case is referred to the
Committee for consideration of the
Senator’s conduct. The Committee’s
report on such a case is submitted to
the Plenary Assembly for decision.

articles.heading: Order during the plenary sitting (1) Senators observe order while attending the plenary sitting
articles.text:
(2) Where Senators engage in disruptive
shouting during the proceedings of the
Plenary Assembly, the presiding officer
for the plenary sitting calls them to
order. If they persist, he or she suspends
the plenary sitting, and Senators
temporarily withdraw from the
Chamber.
(3) The plenary sitting resumes when, in
the opinion of the presiding officer
thereof, order has been restored.
A
148

articles.heading: Disruption, by Senator, of order in Standing Committee (1) Where a Senator disrupts order in a
articles.text:
Standing Committee, the chairperson of
the Committee calls the Senator to order
by naming him or her. In the event of a
repeat act of misconduct, he or she issues
a warning to him or her, which is recorded
in the report of the meeting of the
Standing Committee.
(2) Where the Senator persists or commits
another serious act of misconduct, a
special report is prepared and submitted
to the Bureau of the Senate.

articles.heading: Effects of temporary order requiring a Senator to vacate his or her place and of suspension from attendance
articles.text:
(1) The temporary order requiring a
Senator from his or her seat during the
plenary sitting precludes his or her
participation in decision-making at
the sitting then in progress.
(2) The suspension of a Senator from
attending a plenary sitting precludes
his or her participation in the
proceedings of the Plenary Assembly
for the remaining duration of the
149
sitting from which the Senator is
suspended.

articles.heading: Effects of a Senator’s refusal to leave his or her seat or comply with suspension from attendance
articles.text:
(1) Where a Senator who is subject to
temporary order to leave his or her seat or
suspension from attending the plenary
sitting then in progress fails to comply
with the measure imposed against him or
her, the presiding officer suspends or
adjourns the sitting.
(2) The Senator is definitively suspended
from attending the next three sittings, is
issued a written reprimand, and is
prohibited from attending three meetings
of a Standing Committee, of the
Committee, or of the Conference of
Chairpersons, where the Senator holds
membership therein.

articles.heading: Relief of Senator from temporary order to leave his or her seat or from suspension from attendance
articles.text:
(1) A Senator subject to a temporary order to
leave his or her seat or to suspension from
attendance may submit a written apology
seeking relief from the disciplinary
150
sanctions then in force against him or her.
(2) Where a Senator subject to a temporary
order to leave his or her seat or to
suspension from attendance tenders an
apology prior to the adjournment of the
sitting at which the disciplinary measure
is imposed, the presiding officer for the
plenary sitting reads the apology to those
present at the plenary sitting for the
Plenary Assembly to decide thereon.

articles.heading: Lifting of Senator’s suspension from attending the plenary sitting The suspension of a Senator from attending
articles.text:
the plenary sitting is lifted where –
(a) the Senator subject to suspension
from attendance tenders a written
apology to the Plenary Assembly, the
same being accepted by the latter; or
(b) the Plenary Assembly resolves to
withdraw the suspension.
151

articles.heading: Effects of Senator’s absence from the business of organs of the Senate without reasonable excuse
articles.text:
(1) Where a Senator has been absent from the
business of organs of the Senate without
reasonable excuse, the Bureau of the
Senate refers his or her case to the
Committee for consideration.
(2) The report of the Committee on the case
of a Senator having been absent from the
business of organs of the Senate without
reasonable excuse is submitted to the
Plenary Assembly for decision.
(3) The Plenary Assembly may decide to
issue a warning to a Senator who has been
absent from the business of the organs of
the Senate without reasonable excuse.
The decision of the Plenary Assembly is
notified in writing to the Senator
concerned.
(4) Where a Senator having received a
warning engages in further misconduct,
he or she is liable to one of the following
sanctions:
(a) public reprimand;
152
(b) expulsion from the Senate, subject to
approval by three-fifths of the
members of the Senate.

articles.heading: Instituting proceedings challenging a decision of expulsion from the Senate A Senator who has been expelled from the
articles.text:
Senate in accordance with the provisions of
Articles 130 and 138 of this Organic Law
may institute proceedings before the
competent court challenging that decision.

articles.heading: Prohibited contract for a Senator A Senator may not enter into a public procurement contract with the Government, a
articles.text:
foreign State, or an international
organisation.

articles.heading: Recusal by a Senator in the event of his or her being personally concerned by an issue under consideration
articles.text:
(1) A Senator refrains from any act likely
to compromise the independence and
impartiality required in the
performance of his or her duties.
153
(2) Where a Senator becomes aware that
he or she is personally and
particularly concerned by an item
under consideration by the Senate,
whether in a Standing Committee or
in the plenary sitting, he or she
informs the chair of the meeting of the
Standing Committee or of the plenary
sitting and recuses himself or herself
from the consideration of the item.
Section 2: Senatorial immunity

articles.heading: Senatorial immunity (1) No Senator shall be subject to prosecution, investigation, arrest, detention, or trial in respect of opinions
articles.text:
expressed or votes cast in the course of
his or her duties.
(2) No Senator shall be subject to
prosecution, arrest, or detention in respect
of a felony or misdemeanour, except with
the prior authorisation of the Senate,
given by a two-thirds majority of the
votes of the Senators present at the
plenary sitting, save in cases he or she is
caught red-handed in respect of a felony
or misdemeanour following his or her
155

articles.heading: Immunity card
Request for authorisation to prosecute a Senator (1) A request by the Prosecutor General seeking authorisation to prosecute or
articles.text:
arrest a Senator is submitted in writing to
the President of the Senate.
(2) Such written request specifies, at least,
the names of the Senator as they appear
on his or her national identity card, the
offence of which he or she is suspected,
the classification of that offence, the
place and date of its commission, and the
signature of the Prosecutor General. The
written request is referred to the
Committee for the purpose of preparing a
report for submission to the Plenary
Assembly.

articles.heading: Time limit for consideration by the Plenary Assembly of a request from the Prosecutor General
articles.text:
A request from the Prosecutor General for
authorization to prosecute or arrest a Senator
is considered under an expedited procedure.
Where the Senate is in ordinary session, the
request is considered at the first plenary
sitting following the date of its receipt by the
Senate. Where the Senate is not in ordinary
156
session, an extraordinary session is convened
for that purpose.
CHAPTER VII: INVIOLABILITY OF
PARLIAMENT BUILDING

articles.heading: Inviolability and protection of Parliament building (1) The Parliament building is inviolable
articles.text:
(2) The Parliament building is placed under
the protection of the competent security
organ.

articles.heading: Inviolability of the plenary chamber (1) A person other than a Senator or staff member of the Senate may enter the
articles.text:
plenary chamber only through an
entrance designated for that purpose and
occupies the designated seating area,
while observing order and decorum.
Where a plenary sitting open to the public
proceeds to sit in camera, he or she
withdraws from the plenary chamber.
157
(2) No person shall enter the plenary
chamber with any object liable to disrupt
the orderly conduct of the plenary sitting.

articles.heading: Inviolability of the seats reserved for Senators Except for staff members of the Senate who
articles.text:
provide support during the business of the
Plenary Assembly, no person shall enter the
area designated for the seating of Senators
unless authorized by the presiding officer for
the plenary sitting.

articles.heading: Measure against a person other than a Senator for the conduct prejudicial to order and decorum during
articles.text:
plenary sitting
Any member of the public attending the
proceedings of the Plenary Assembly whose
conduct is prejudicial to order and decorum
is expelled from the plenary chamber.

articles.heading: Public notice of the inviolability of the plenary chamber The provisions of this Organic Law relating
articles.text:
to the inviolability of the plenary chamber are
displayed at the entrances to the plenary
158
chamber.
CHAPTER VIII: PROCEDURES FOR
VOTING ON LAWS

articles.heading: Transmission to Senate of Draft Law or Private Member’s Bill (1) The Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies
articles.text:
transmits to the Senate any Draft Law or
Private Member’s Bill adopted by the
Chamber of Deputies that falls within the
Senate’s competence, together with the
accompanying explanatory note and the
minutes of the sitting at which adoption
thereof took place.
(2) A Draft Law or Private Member’s Bill is
submitted to the Senate written in the
official languages in which laws are
drafted.

articles.heading: Transmission of Draft Law or Private Member’s Bill to Senators The President of the Senate transmits to the
articles.text:
Senators the Draft Law or Private Member’s
Bill referred to in Article 151 of this Organic
Law at least seven days prior to the plenary
sitting at which its necessity is to be
approved. However, where reasonable
159
grounds justify urgency, this time limit is
waived.

articles.heading: Approval of the necessity of Draft Law or Private Member’s Bill (1) The Senate considers any Draft Law or
articles.text:
Private Member’s Bill submitted to it for
the purpose of ascertaining its necessity.
(2) When considering the necessity of a
Draft Law or Private Member’s Bill, the
general debate in the plenary sitting
takes place in the presence of the
initiator thereof, who provides
clarifications relating thereto.

articles.heading: Transmission of Draft Law or Private Member’s Bill to Standing Committee and procedures for submission
articles.text:
of amendments
(1) The President of the Senate, following
the approval of the necessity of a Draft
Law or Private Member’s Bill, refers it
to the relevant Standing Committee.
However, the President of the Senate
may, where necessary, refer it to another
Standing Committee.
(2) A Senator proposing an amendment to a
Draft Law or Private Member’s Bill
162

articles.heading: Consideration of Draft Law or Private Member’s Bill at Standing Committee stage
Transmission to Senators of report of Standing Committee on consideration of Draft Law or Private
articles.text:
Member’s Bill
22

articles.heading: Debate on report of Standing Committee on consideration of Draft Law or Private Member’s Bill
articles.text:
(1) Debate in the plenary sitting is conducted,
in the first instance, on the report of the
Standing Committee having considered
the Draft Law or Private Member’s Bill.
(2) Debate covers the provisions not
amended, provisions having been the
subject of editorial amendments, and
provisions having been the subject of
substantive amendments.
(3) Once reported by the Standing
Committee, a Draft Law or Private
Member’s Bill is not open to general
debate in the plenary sitting.
(4) The sponsor of the Draft Law or Private
Member’s Bill is invited to attend the
plenary sitting convened for its adoption.

articles.heading: Vote on Articles of Draft Law or Private Member’s Bill (1) Voting on Articles of a Draft Law or
articles.text:
Private Member’s Bill is conducted by
means of appropriate equipment, a show
of hands, or any other possible method.
163
(2) An Article of a Draft Law or Private
Member’s Bill failing to secure the
requisite majority is provisionally
removed. However, a Senator, the
Standing Committee having considered
the Draft Law or Private Member’s Bill,
or the sponsor thereof may, through the
presiding officer for the plenary sitting,
request the referral of the Article back to
the Standing Committee, subject to the
approval of the Plenary Assembly.

articles.heading: Reconsideration of Article of Draft Law or Private Member’s Bill (1) Where, following debate, the Plenary
articles.text:
Assembly is of the view that an Article
raises issues requiring to be addressed, it
may refer that Article back to the
Standing Committee.
(2) The Standing Committee may request the
referral back to it of an Article not yet put
to the vote for fresh reconsideration. Any
such request is subject to a decision of the
Plenary Assembly.
(3) Until such time as a Draft Law or Private
Member’s Bill has been the subject of a
vote in its entirety by the Plenary
Assembly, the Standing Committee may,
164
at its request or at the request of a Senator,
and subject to approval by the Plenary
Assembly, reconsider an Article
previously adopted by the Plenary
Assembly and report thereon to the
Plenary Assembly for the purpose of
renewed voting thereon.
(4) The report on an Article reconsidered by
the Standing Committee is submitted to
the Senators at least two days prior to its
consideration by the Plenary Assembly.
Where urgency so requires, however,
such time limit is waived.

articles.heading: Vote on Draft Law or Private Member’s Bill in its entirety (1) For the vote on a Draft Law or Private
articles.text:
Member’s Bill in its entirety, voting is
conducted by roll-call of Senators.
(2) During the vote on a Draft Law or Private
Member’s Bill in its entirety, the roll-call
vote is conducted by the Clerk or, in the
event of his or her absence, by his or her
substitute, by calling the names of Senators
in alphabetical order, as recorded on their
national identity cards. Where neither of
them is available, the Bureau of the Senate
designates another staff member of the
Senate to perform that function.
165
(3) During the vote on a Draft Law or Private
Member’s Bill in its entirety, any person,
upon the calling of his or her name,
records his or her vote orally by stating
aloud “Aye”, “No”, or “I abstain”. Where,
however, a Senator whose name is called
is unable to speak, he or she records his
or her vote, by any other possible means.
(4) The vote on a Draft Law or Private
Member’s Bill in its entirety is
determined by the majority specified in
the Constitution of the Republic of
Rwanda.

articles.heading: Transmission to Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies of Law adopted by the Senate (1) Where a Law is adopted by the Senate
articles.text:
without amendment, the President of the
Senate transmits it to the Speaker of the
Chamber of Deputies.
(2) Where a Law is adopted by the Senate
with amendments, the President of the
Senate transmits it to the Speaker of the
Chamber of Deputies, together with a
brief statement of the amendments made.
166
(3) Where a Law is not adopted, the
President of the Senate returns it to the
Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies,
together with a brief statement of the
reasons for its rejection.

articles.heading: Verification of conformity of text of Law as published in the Official Gazette of the Republic of Rwanda with
articles.text:
the text of Law adopted by the Plenary
Assembly
(1) The Bureau of the Senate ascertains the
conformity between the text of the Law
as published in the Republic of Rwanda and the text of the
Law adopted by the Plenary Assembly.
(2) Where it is determined that the text of the
Law published in the the Republic of Rwanda is not in full
conformity with the text of the Law
adopted by the Plenary Assembly, the
President of the Senate informs the
Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies
thereof, for him or her to inform the
relevant organs thereof.
167

articles.heading: Revision of the Constitution of the Republic of Rwanda initiated by the Senate (1) Where the initiative for the revision of the
articles.text:
Constitution of the Republic of Rwanda
originates in the Senate, such an initiative
is approved by a majority of at least twothirds of the members of the Senate. The
proposal for revision, having been
approved by the Senate as to its necessity,
is transmitted to the Chamber of
Deputies. Following its adoption by the
Chamber of Deputies, the proposal for
revision is referred back to the Senate.
(2) Final adoption of a revision of the
Constitution of the Republic of Rwanda
requires a majority of at least threequarters of the members of the Senate, as
provided for under the Constitution of the
Republic of Rwanda.

articles.heading: Compliance with this Organic Law in cases of urgency In cases of urgency, the provisions of this
articles.text:
Organic Law governing the order of business,
translation, or time limits may be derogated
from, either at the request of the Government
or by decision of the Senate made at the
request of a Senator.
168

articles.heading: Expedited consideration of Draft Law or Private Member’s Bill (1) A request for expedited consideration of
articles.text:
a Draft Law or Private Member’s Bill,
where initiated by a Senator, is subject to
approval by a majority of two-thirds of
the Senators present at the plenary
sitting. A request initiated by the
Government is granted where reasonable
grounds are established.
(2) Where a request for expedited
consideration of a Draft Law or Private
Member’s Bill is granted, its
consideration is accorded priority on the
order of business.

articles.heading: Request for and decision on adoption of Draft Law or Private Member’s Bill without referral to
articles.text:
Standing Committee
Where the Plenary Assembly has approved
the necessity of a Draft Law or Private
Member’s Bill, the sponsor thereof may
request its direct adoption without referral to
a Standing Committee. Any such request is
decided by a vote of at least three-fifths of the
Senators present at the plenary sitting.
169
CHAPTER IX: METHODS EMPLOYED
BY THE SENATE IN DISCHARGE OF
ITS EXCLUSIVE RESPONSIBILITIES
AND OF ITS POWERS
Section One: Methods employed in
monitoring application of fundamental
principles

articles.heading: Methods employed by the Senate in monitoring the application of fundamental principles (1) The Senate monitors the application of
articles.text:
the fundamental principles whenever it
discharges its responsibilities or exercises
its powers.
(2) For the purpose of monitoring the
application of the fundamental principles,
the Senate employs the following
methods:
(a) analysis of documents;
(b) exchange of views with a member
of the Government;
(c) consultative meetings;
(d) the conduct of research;
170
(e) public outreach visits.
Section 2: Monitoring the functioning of
political organisations

articles.heading: Procedures for monitoring the functioning of a political organisation Whenever necessary, the competent Standing
articles.text:
Committee conducts the monitoring of the
functioning of a political organisation
lawfully constituted in Rwanda and prepares
a report for submission to the President of the
Senate.

articles.heading: Initiation of accountability proceedings and the seeking of action against a political organisation
articles.text:
The Senate initiates accountability
proceedings against a political organisation
in the event of serious failure to comply with
the obligations set out in Articles 10, 56, 57
and 58 of the Constitution of the Republic of
Rwanda.
171

articles.heading: Seeking of action against a political organisation The Senate, having regard to the gravity of
articles.text:
the act of misconduct observed on the part of
a political organisation, may request the
organ in charge of political organisations to
take, in respect of that political organisation,
any of the actions provided for under Article
59 of the Constitution of the Republic of
Rwanda, subject to approval by the Plenary
Assembly by a three-fifths majority of the
Senators present.
Section 3: Procedures for approving the
appointment of officials

articles.heading: Submission to the Senate of names and biographical file of an official whose approval of appointment is
articles.text:
requested
(1) The Government submits to the Senate
the names and biographical file of an
official provided for under the
Constitution of the Republic of Rwanda
and any other Law for approval of his or
her appointment.
(2) The President of the Senate submits the
biographical file of an official to the
172
relevant Standing Committee for
consideration.

articles.heading: Consideration of biographical file and approval of appointment of official (1) In the course of considering an
articles.text:
official’s biographical file, the
Standing Committee may invite to its
meetings an official whose approval
of appointment is requested, or any
other person capable of furnishing it
with the clarifications needed.
(2) The Standing Committee having
considered the biographical file
submits its report to the Plenary
Assembly for decision thereon by an
absolute majority of the votes of the
Senators present at the plenary sitting.
CHAPTER X: RELATIONS BETWEEN
THE SENATE AND THE CHAMBER OF
DEPUTIES
Section One: Joint business of both
Chambers of Parliament
173

articles.heading: Holding of joint sitting of both Chambers of Parliament (1) Both Chambers of Parliament convene in
articles.text:
joint sitting in the circumstances provided
for under the Constitution of the Republic
of Rwanda or other Laws.
(2) Both Chambers of Parliament may also
convene in joint sitting to consider a
matter of public interest, after
consultation between their respective
Bureaus and subject to approval by the
Plenary Assembly of each Chamber of
Parliament.
(3) The joint sitting of both Chambers of
Parliament is presided over by the
Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies or,
in his or her absence, by the President of
the Senate.
(4) When both Chambers of Parliament
convene in joint sitting, the presence of at
least two members of the Bureau of, and
the quorum applicable to, each Chamber
of Parliament are required.
174

articles.heading: Convening of both Chambers of Parliament in extraordinary session (1) Both Chambers of Parliament may be
articles.text:
convened in extraordinary session after
consultation between their respective
Presiding Officers or at the request of the
President of the Republic or of onequarter of the members of each Chamber
of Parliament.
(2) The programme of business for the
extraordinary session is prepared after
consultation between the Bureaus of both
Chambers of Parliament and adopted by
the members of the Plenary Assembly of
each Chamber of Parliament present at
the first sitting of the extraordinary
session.
(3) The Presiding Officer of each Chamber of
Parliament convenes the members of that
Chamber to an extraordinary session.
175

articles.heading: Presentation of report of a National Commission or specialized organ at a joint sitting of both Chambers of
articles.text:
Parliament
(1) Any National Commission or specialized
organ required, under the Constitution of
the Republic of Rwanda or other Laws, to
submit reports to Parliament submits such
reports in writing to the Presiding
Officers of both Chambers of Parliament.
(2) When both Chambers of Parliament
convene in joint sitting to be presented
with a report, the head of the National
Commission or of the specialized organ,
or, in his or her absence, his or her deputy,
is granted the floor to briefly present the
contents of the report.
(3) Members of Parliament are entitled to
seek clarifications on the contents of the
report.
(4) Following the presentation of the report
of a National Commission or a
specialized organ to a joint sitting of both
Chambers of Parliament, the relevant
Presiding Officer of the Chamber refers
the report to the Standing Committee
176
within whose portfolio it falls.
(5) The Standing Committee of each
Chamber of Parliament to which the
report of a National Commission or
specialized organ is referred considers the
report and prepares a report thereon.
(6) The Plenary Assembly of each Chamber
of Parliament considers the draft
resolutions of the Standing Committee
having considered the report for decision
thereon. Resolutions adopted are
transmitted to the relevant organs.
(7) The Plenary Assembly of each Chamber
of Parliament may request a report on a
specific matter falling within the
competence of a National Commission or
of a specialized organ.

articles.heading: Law applicable in the event of a joint sitting of both Chambers of Parliament (1) In the event of a joint sitting of both
articles.text:
Chambers of Parliament, the Organic
Law governing the functioning of the
Chamber of Deputies applies.
177
(2) In a joint sitting of both Chambers of
Parliament, a Senator has the same rights
and obligations as those provided for
under this Organic Law for a Deputy.

articles.heading: Minutes and Hansard reports of joint sitting of both Chambers of Parliament (1) Minutes and Hansard reports are drawn
articles.text:
up for a joint sitting of both Chambers of
Parliament.
(2) Minutes of a joint sitting of both
Chambers of Parliament are adopted in
accordance with the procedures
applicable to the adoption of the minutes
of the presiding Chamber of Parliament.
(3) The Plenary Assembly of the presiding
Chamber of Parliament adopts the
Hansard report of a joint sitting of both
Chambers of Parliament in accordance
with the procedures and time limits
provided for under the Organic Law
determining the functioning of that
Chamber.
178
(4) The Presiding Officer of the presiding
Chamber of Parliament transmits, by
electronic means, the Hansard report of
the joint sitting of both Chambers of
Parliament to the Presiding Officer of the
other Chamber, who in turn transmits it to
the members of the Plenary Assembly of
his or her Chamber.
(5) A Deputy or Senator who seeks to make
a correction to the Hansard report submits
it in writing to the Presiding Officer of the
Chamber of which he or she is a member,
who in turn transmits it to the Presiding
Officer of the Chamber of Parliament
having presided over the sitting.
(6) The adopted Hansard report of a joint
sitting of both Chambers of Parliament is
jointly signed by the presiding officer for
the sitting and the Clerk of the presiding
Chamber of Parliament. A copy thereof is
transmitted to the other Chamber of
Parliament.

articles.heading: Provision of opinions on the budget framework paper and Draft Law determining State finances
articles.text:
(1) The Senate provides the Chamber of
179
Deputies with opinions on the budget
framework paper and on the Draft Law
determining State finances prior to their
final adoption by the Chamber of
Deputies.
(2) The President of the Senate refers the
budget framework paper and the Draft
Law determining State finances to the
Standing Committee in charge of State
finances for consideration, and the
Committee prepares draft opinions for
approval by the Plenary Assembly and
subsequent submission to the Chamber of
Deputies.

articles.heading: Joint Committee of both Chambers of Parliament (1) Where the Senate rejects a Draft Law or Private Member’s Bill, or where
articles.text:
amendments made thereto by the Senate
are not approved by the Chamber of
Deputies, a Joint Committee of both
Chambers of Parliament is established,
composed of five Deputies and five
Senators, to propose a compromise on the
disputed provisions.
(2) A Joint Committee of both Chambers of
Parliament may also be established,
180
subject to approval by the Plenary
Assembly of each Chamber of Parliament
by a three-fifths majority of its members,
to deliberate on any other issue identified
in a Law adopted by both Chambers,
provided that such Law has not yet been
transmitted for publication.
(3) The Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies
transmits to the President of the Senate
the names of the Deputies designated to
that effect, together with a memorandum
setting out the grounds on which the
Chamber of Deputies has rejected the
Senate’s resolution.
(4) Within seven days of receipt of such names,
the President of the Senate notifies the
Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies of the
names of five Senators designated to sit on
the Joint Committee of both Chambers of
Parliament.
(5) The first meeting of the Joint Committee of
both Chambers of Parliament is convened
in writing after consultation between the
lead members of the groups. At that
meeting, the members of the Joint
Committee elect, from among their
number, a chairperson and a vice
chairperson.
181

articles.heading: Report of Joint Committee of both Chambers of Parliament (1) The report setting out the compromise
articles.text:
text agreed upon by the Joint Committee
of both Chambers of Parliament is
submitted to each Chamber for a vote
thereon, without the possibility of further
amendment.
(2) Where the Joint Committee of both
Chambers of Parliament fails to reach a
compromise, or where the proposed
compromise is rejected by both
Chambers or by either Chamber of
Parliament, the draft law or private
Member’s bill is referred back to the
initiator thereof.
(3) Where a Draft Law or Private Member’s
Bill has been referred back to its initiator
in the cases provided for under Paragraph
(2) of this Article, the initiator may
reintroduce it at any time.
(4) Where the initiator of a Draft Law or
Private Member’s Bill reintroduces it, he
or she submits it to the Speaker of the
Chamber of Deputies.
182
(5) Where, at the time of presentation of a
report in the plenary sitting, the lead
member of a group is unavailable, the
report is presented by the eldest Senator
among the members of the group.

articles.heading: Procedures applicable to request for withdrawal of Draft Law or Private Member’s Bill made by its initiator
articles.text:
The initiator of a Draft Law or Private
Member’s Bill may, at any stage thereof,
submit a request for its withdrawal. A person
who requests the withdrawal of a Draft Law or
Private Member’s Bill makes his or her request
in writing through the Speaker of the Chamber
of Deputies, who submits a written request for
withdrawal thereof to the President of the
Senate. The Plenary Assembly decides thereon
once the necessity of the Draft Law or Private
Member’s Bill has been approved.

articles.heading: Transmission to President of the Republic of Law adopted by the Senate The Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies
articles.text:
exercises the exclusive authority to transmit to
the President of the Republic any law adopted
by the Senate for promulgation before its
publication.
183

articles.heading: Second reading of Law at the request of the President of the Republic (1) Where a Law in respect of which a
articles.text:
request for a second reading has been
made falls within the competence of the
Senate, the Speaker of the Chamber of
Deputies transmits it to the President of
the Senate, together with the relevant
minutes of the Plenary Assembly, for
consideration by the Senate.
(2) Where a request for a second reading of a
Law has been made, the President of the
Senate refers it to the relevant Standing
Committee for the preparation of a report
for the Plenary Assembly and informs all
Senators thereof.
Section 2: Networks or forums or national
chapters of international networks or
forums of Deputies and Senators

articles.heading: Establishment of network or forum or of national chapter of an international network or forum bringing
articles.text:
together Deputies and Senators
A network or forum or national chapter of an
international network or forum bringing
together Deputies and Senators may be
184
constituted in accordance with the legal
provisions governing each Chamber of
Parliament.

articles.heading: Request for, and approval of, the establishment of network or forum or of national chapter of an international
articles.text:
network or forum bringing together
Deputies and Senators
(1) The establishment of a network or forum
or of a national chapter of an international
network or forum bringing together
Deputies and Senators may be requested
by at least five Deputies and at least three
Senators.
(2) The establishment of a network or forum
or of a national chapter of an international
network or forum bringing together
Deputies and Senators is subject to
approval by the Plenary Assembly of
each Chamber of Parliament.
(3) A letter requesting the establishment of a
network or forum, or of a national chapter
of an international network or forum
bringing together Deputies and Senators,
together with a concept note setting out
its mission and programme, is submitted
to the Presiding Officer of each Chamber
of Parliament and is subject to agreement
185
between the Bureaus of both Chambers,
prior to its placement on the order of
business of the Plenary Assembly of each
Chamber of Parliament.
(4) The authors of a request for the
establishment of a network or forum, or
of a national chapter of an international
network or forum, elect from among their
number a Senator or a Deputy to provide
clarifications on it before the Plenary
Assembly of the Chamber to which that
member belongs.

articles.heading: Statutes of network or forum or national chapter of an international network or forum bringing together
articles.text:
Deputies and Senators
(1) A network or forum or a national chapter
of an international network or forum
bringing together Deputies and Senators
establishes its governing statutes.
(2) The statutes of a network or forum or of a
national chapter of an international
network or forum bringing together
Deputies and Senators specify at least the
following:
186
(a) the objectives of the network or
forum, or of a national chapter of an
international network or forum
bringing together Deputies and
Senators, and its duration;
(b) conditions for membership of the
network or forum, or of a national
chapter of an international network or
forum bringing together Deputies and
Senators;
(c) the organs of the network or forum, or
of a national chapter of an
international network or forum
bringing together Deputies and
Senators;
(d) the source of finances of the network
or forum, or of a national chapter of
an international network or forum
bringing together Deputies and
Senators;
(e) the functioning of the network or
forum, or of a national chapter of an
international network or forum
bringing together Deputies and
Senators;
(f) relations between the network or
forum, or a national chapter of an
187
international network or forum
bringing together Deputies and
Senators, and other organs;
(g) the provisions governing the
dissolution of the network or forum,
or of a national chapter of an
international network or forum
bringing together Deputies and
Senators.

articles.heading: Adoption of the statutes and election of office-bearers of network or forum or national chapter of an
articles.text:
international network or forum
(1) Following approval by the Plenary
Assembly of each Chamber of Parliament
of the establishment of a network or
forum, or of a national chapter of an
international network or forum bringing
together Deputies and Senators, the first
meeting of the network or forum, or of the
national chapter, adopts the statutes and
proceeds to the election of its officebearers.
(2) The launch of a network or forum, or of a
national chapter of an international
network or forum bringing together
Deputies and Senators, together with its
188
constituent instruments, is notified to the
Presiding Officers of both Chambers of
Parliament.

articles.heading: Decision establishing network or forum, or national chapter of an international network or forum bringing
articles.text:
together Deputies and Senators
The decision establishing a network or
forum, or a national chapter of an
international network or forum and indicating
its representatives, is jointly signed by the
Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies and the
President of the Senate.

articles.heading: Activity report of network or forum or of national chapter of an international network or forum bringing
articles.text:
together Deputies and Senators
(1) Each quarter and whenever necessary, a
network or forum, or a national chapter of
an international network or forum
bringing together Deputies and Senators
submits its activity programme and
activity report to the Presiding Officer of
each Chamber of Parliament.
(2) After receipt of the activity report, the
189
Presiding Officer of each Chamber
transmits it to the members of his or her
Chamber.
(3) Where the activity report identifies
matters capable of giving rise to a
decision, the Bureaus of both Chambers
of Parliament agree on the course of
action.

articles.heading: Supervision over a network or forum or a national chapter of an international network or forum bringing
articles.text:
together Deputies and Senators
(1) Following agreement between the
Bureaus of both Chambers of Parliament,
each network or forum, or each national
chapter of an international network or
forum bringing together Deputies and
Senators, is placed under the supervision
of either Chamber of Parliament.
(2) Each Chamber of Parliament makes
provision, in its budget, for an annual
financial allocation for a network or
forum, or for a national chapter of an
international network or forum, placed
under its supervision.
(3) Each year, and whenever necessary, the
Clerk prepares a report on the use of the
190
finances of a network or forum, or of a
national chapter of an international
network or forum bringing together
Deputies and Senators, placed under the
supervision of the Senate, and transmits it
to the President of the Senate, with a copy
to the Speaker of the Chamber of
Deputies and to the leadership of the
network or forum, or of the chapter of an
international network or forum.

articles.heading: Monitoring of functioning of network or forum or of national chapter of an international network or forum
articles.text:
bringing together Deputies and Senators
The Bureaus of both Chambers of Parliament
monitor the functioning of a network or forum,
or of a national chapter of an international
network or forum bringing together Deputies
and Senators, in accordance with the Organic
Law determining the functioning of each
Chamber of Parliament.

articles.heading: Dissolution of network or forum or of national chapter of an international network or forum bringing
articles.text:
together Deputies and Senators
(1) A network or forum, or a national chapter
of an international network or forum
bringing together Deputies and Senators,
191
may be dissolved where it acts in
contradiction with the mission or the
functioning of Parliament, or where the
grounds for its establishment have ceased
to exist.
(2) A request for the dissolution of a network
or forum, or of a national chapter of an
international network or forum bringing
together Deputies and Senators, may be
made by –
(a) One-third of the members of the
network or forum, or of the national
chapter of an international network or
forum bringing together Deputies and
Senators;
(b) at least five Deputies or three Senators,
not being members of the network or
forum, or of the national chapter of an
international network or forum
bringing together Deputies and
Senators;
(c) the General Assembly of the network
or forum, or of the national chapter of
an international network or forum
bringing together Deputies and
Senators.
(3) The authors of a request for the
192
dissolution of a network or forum, or of a
national chapter of an international
network or forum bringing together
Deputies and Senators, submit the request
in writing to the Presiding Officers of
both Chambers of Parliament.
(4) A request for the dissolution of a network
or forum, or of a national chapter of an
international network or forum bringing
together Deputies and Senators, is
considered by the Bureaus of both
Chambers of Parliament.
(5) A decision to dissolve a network or
forum, or a national chapter of an
international network or forum bringing
together Deputies and Senators, is made
by the Plenary Assembly of each
Chamber of Parliament.
(6) Where either Chamber of Parliament
adopts a decision to dissolve a network or
forum, or an international network or
forum bringing together Deputies and
Senators, such decision has the effect of
dissolving the network or forum, or the
national chapter of the international
network or forum.
193
Section 3: Joint parliamentary friendship
group

articles.heading: Establishment, members and leadership of joint parliamentary friendship group (1) The Bureaus of both Chambers of
articles.text:
Parliament decide the establishment of a
joint parliamentary friendship group
which maintains relationships with
Parliament of a country whose
Parliament is bicameral.
(2) The Bureaus of both Chambers of
Parliament agree on members and
office-bearers of the joint parliamentary
friendship group and agree upon the
Chamber of Parliament under whose
supervision the group is placed.
194

articles.heading: Activity programme and activity report of joint parliamentary friendship group Each joint parliamentary friendship group
articles.text:
submits its activity programme and activity
report to the Presiding Officer of each
Chamber of Parliament.

articles.heading: Matters not provided for under this Organic Law relating to relations between both Chambers of
articles.text:
Parliament
(1) Relations between both Chambers of
Parliament are governed by the Organic
Law determining the functioning of each
Chamber of Parliament.
(2) Where a matter concerning both
Chambers of Parliament is not provided
for under this Organic Law, the Bureaus
of both Chambers of Parliament agree on
the procedures for its resolution.
Where recourse to a resolution of the
Plenary Assembly is required, the matter
is referred to the Plenary Assembly of
each Chamber of Parliament for decision.
195
CHAPTER XI: RELATIONS BETWEEN
PARLIAMENT AND OTHER
LEGISLATURES

articles.heading: Election of representatives of Rwanda to international interparliamentary bodies (1) Each Chamber of Parliament elects, in
articles.text:
accordance with the relevant legislation,
representatives of Rwanda to an interparliamentary entity of which the
Parliament of Rwanda is a member.
(2) Upon the expiry of the term of office of
the Senators, or upon the dissolution of
the Chamber of Deputies, the
representatives elected to represent
Rwanda to the inter-parliamentary body
of which the Parliament of Rwanda is a
member forfeit their representative status
within that body.

articles.heading: Provision of opinions on a bill or document of the East African Legislative Assembly (1) After receipt of a bill or other document
articles.text:
196
debated by the East African Legislative
Assembly, the Clerks of the Chambers of
Parliament transmit the same to the
Presiding Officers of both Chambers of
Parliament.
(2) The Presiding Officer of each Chamber of
Parliament refers the bill or document to
the members of the Standing Committee
in charge of matters related to such a bill
or document fall.
(3) The Standing Committees of both
Chambers of Parliament competent in
that regard jointly consider the bill or
document emanating from the East
African Legislative Assembly.
(4) The Standing Committees in charge of
matters related to the bill or document
referred to in Paragraph (1) of this Article
may request the invitation of the Minister
in charge of East African Community
Affairs to provide them with such
clarifications as are needed.
197
(5) If considered necessary, the Minister in
charge of East African Community affairs
may be invited to participate in the
plenary sitting of the Chamber
concerned.
(6) The Standing Committees consider the
bill or any other document referred to in
this Article and agree on a report for
submission to the Plenary Assembly of
each Chamber of Parliament. The agreedupon report is adopted in the plenary
sitting of each Chamber of Parliament.
(7) The Clerks of both Chambers of
Parliament, by means of a jointly signed
letter, transmit to the Clerk of the East
African Legislative Assembly all
documents and decisions containing
opinions of Parliament, in accordance
with the Treaty for the Establishment of
the East African Community.
198

articles.heading: Consideration of document emanating from another legislature or from any other organisation of which
articles.text:
Parliament of Rwanda is a member
(1) The Presiding Officer of each Chamber of
Parliament, by written notice, refers to
the relevant Standing Committee any
matter relating to a document emanating
from another legislature or from any
other organisation of which Parliament of
Rwanda is a member.
(2) Where it appears that a decision may be
required of the Plenary Assembly in
respect of such a document, the Bureaus
of both Chambers of Parliament, on the
basis of the report, agree on the course of
action to be taken. Where approval by the
Plenary Assembly is required, such
approval is given separately by each
Chamber of Parliament.

articles.heading: Establishment of relationships with a legislature of another State or with international inter-parliamentary
articles.text:
organisation
The establishment of relationships between
Parliament of Rwanda and a legislature of
199
another foreign State or international interparliamentary organisations is conducted in
accordance with the national foreign affairs
policy through:
(a) an international meeting convening
members of Parliament of Rwanda
and representatives of an
international inter-parliamentary
organisation;
(b) a parliamentary friendship group
bringing together members of
Parliament of Rwanda and members
of the legislature of another State;
(c) a visit by a member of Parliament of
Rwanda to the legislature of another
State, or the latter’s invitation of a
representative of such legislature;
(d) the conclusion of a memorandum of
understanding with another
legislature.
CHAPTER XII: MANAGEMENT OF
SENATE FINANCES
200

articles.heading: Budget of the Senate (1) The Senate has its own budget and enjoys financial autonomy
articles.text:
(2) Funds appropriated under the budget
of the Senate are used in accordance
with the relevant legislation.

articles.heading: Adoption of draft budget of the Senate (1) The Office of the Clerk prepares the draft budget proposal of the Senate, which is
articles.text:
submitted to the Standing Committee in
charge of budgetary matters for
consideration and report to the Plenary
Assembly.
(2) The Vice President of the Senate in
charge of financial affairs and the Clerk
act jointly in concurring with the Minister
in charge of finance on the draft budget of
the Senate following its adoption by the
Plenary Assembly.

articles.heading: Audit of the use of the budget of the Senate The audit of the use of the budget of the 201
articles.text:
Senate is conducted by the Office of the
Auditor General of State Finances.
CHAPTER XIII: MISCELLANEOUS
PROVISIONS

articles.heading: Language used by a Senator to express his or her opinions In expressing his or her opinions, whether
articles.text:
orally or in writing, a Senator uses one of the
recognised official languages of his or her
choice.

articles.heading: Resolution of a matter not provided for under this Organic Law Where a matter arises relating to the
articles.text:
functioning of the Senate that is not provided
for under this Organic Law or other Laws, the
Bureau of the Senate provides guidance for
its resolution. Where the Bureau of the Senate
considers that the matter requires a resolution
of the Plenary Assembly, it places it on the
order of business of the Plenary Assembly.

articles.heading: Proposal to amend this Organic Law A proposal to amend this Organic Law is initiated by the Senate which submits it to the
articles.text:
Chamber of Deputies for consideration.
202

articles.text: repealed.

ADOPTS:
CHAPTER ONE: GENERAL
PROVISIONS

articles.heading: Objet de la présente loi organique
Sénat
Modalités d’élection ou de nomination d’un sénateur L’élection ou la nomination d’un sénateur se
articles.text:
fait conformément aux dispositions de la
Constitution de la République du Rwanda et
d’autres lois.

articles.heading: Attributions du Sénat (1) Le Sénat a les attributions suivantes
articles.text:
(a) débattre des lois, voter des lois et
légiférer ;
(b) contrôler l’action du
Gouvernement.
(2) Le Sénat a également les attributions
exclusives suivantes :
(a) assurer le suivi de l’application des
principes fondamentaux suivants
prévus par la Constitution de la
République du Rwanda :
(i) prévention et répression du crime
de génocide, lutte contre le
négationnisme et révisionnisme
du génocide ainsi que
l’éradication de l’idéologie du
génocide et toutes ses
manifestations ;
(ii) éradication des discriminations et
divisions fondées sur l’ethnie, la
région ou tout autre motif et la
promotion de l’unité nationale ;
(iii) partage équitable du pouvoir ;
(iv) édification d’un État de droit et
d’un régime démocratique
pluraliste, égalité de tous les
Rwandais et égalité entre les
femmes et les hommes reflétée par
l’attribution aux femmes d’au
moins 30% des postes dans les
instances de prise de décisions ;
(v) édification d’un État œuvrant à la
promotion du bien-être de la
population et création de
mécanismes appropriés pour
faciliter l’accès à la justice
sociale ;
(vi) recherche constante de solutions
par la voie du dialogue et du
consensus.
(b) assurer le suivi du fonctionnement des
formations politiques ;
(c) fournir à la Chambre des Députés ses
avis sur le document-cadre budgétaire
et sur le projet de loi portant fixation
des finances de l’État avant son
adoption définitive.

articles.heading: Compétences du Sénat (1) En matière législative, le Sénat est compétent pour voter  (a) la révision de la Constitution de la
articles.text:
République du Rwanda ;
(b) les lois organiques ;
(c) les lois portant approbation de la
ratification des traités et accords
internationaux sur –
(i) l’armistice ;
(ii) la paix ;
(iii) la modification des lois
nationales ;
(iv) l’état des personnes ;
(v) la création d’une organisation
internationale.
(d) les lois approuvant l’adhésion du
Rwanda aux traités et accords
internationaux relatifs à une
organisation internationale ;
(e) les lois sur la défense et la sécurité
nationale.
(2) Le Sénat est également investi des
pouvoirs de :
(a) approuver la nomination des autorités
prévues par la Constitution de la
République du Rwanda et par d’autres
lois ;
(b) fournir des conseils sur des questions
d’importance nationale majeure
relevant de ses attributions.

articles.heading: Fonctions incompatibles avec celle de sénateur (1) Les fonctions incompatibles avec la fonction de sénateur sont celles de
Démission d’une fonction incompatible avec la qualité de sénateur Sauf pour les fonctions visées au paragraphe
articles.text:
(1)(f)(g)(h)(p) de l’article 6 de la présente loi
organique, l’exercice de toute autre fonction
incompatible avec celle de sénateur n’empêche
pas son titulaire d’être élu ou nommé sénateur.
Toutefois, dès sa prestation de serment, ce
sénateur démissionne immédiatement, par
écrit, de sa fonction antérieure et en informe le
Président du Sénat et l’Ombudsman.

articles.heading: Prestation de serment et entrée en fonction d’un sénateur Avant d’entrer en fonction, un sénateur prête
articles.text:
publiquement, devant le Président de la
République ou, en son absence, devant le
Président de la Cour Suprême, le serment
prévu par la Constitution de la République du
Rwanda.

articles.heading: Mandat d’un sénateur (1) Un sénateur élu ou nommé exerce un mandat de cinq ans, renouvelable une fois
articles.text:
(2) Un sénateur ancien Chef d’État n’est pas
soumis à la limitation du nombre de
mandats.

articles.heading: Déclaration de patrimoine Chaque sénateur soumet à l’Office de l’Ombudsman une déclaration écrite de
articles.text:
patrimoine conformément à la législation en la
matière.

articles.heading: Vacance du siège d’un sénateur Le siège d’un sénateur devient vacant lorsqu’il– (a) démissionne ;
articles.text:
(b) est démis de ses fonctions par décision
judiciaire ;
(c) est, pour quelque raison que ce soit,
définitivement empêché d’exercer ses
fonctions ; ou
(d) décède.

articles.heading: Démission d’un sénateur de son mandat Un sénateur qui démissionne de son mandat de sénateur adresse sa lettre de démission au
articles.text:
Président du Sénat qui, dans les sept jours à
compter de la réception de ladite lettre, en
informe le Président de la République, le
Président de la Chambre des Députés et le
Président de la Cour suprême. Cette démission
est également portée à la connaissance de la
population par voie d’annonce dans les médias
et sur le site web du Sénat.

articles.heading: Remplacement d’un sénateur (1) Lorsqu’un sénateur élu cesse d’exercer son mandat pour l’un quelconque des motifs
articles.text:
prévus par la présente loi organique, il est
remplacé conformément aux dispositions
de la loi organique régissant les élections.
Lorsqu’il s’agit d’un sénateur nommé,
l’organe qui l’a nommé procède à la
désignation de son successeur.
(2) Lorsqu’un sénateur cesse d’exercer son
mandat, le Président du Sénat demande,
dans un délai de 30 jours, à l’organe qui l’a
nommé ou, s’il s’agit d’un sénateur élu, à
la Commission électorale nationale, de
pourvoir à son remplacement.
(3) Un nouveau sénateur ainsi élu ou nommé
exerce son mandat pour la durée restant à
courir de celui de son prédécesseur. Il peut
être renommé ou réélu pour un nouveau
mandat.
CHAPITRE II : ORGANISATION DU
SÉNAT

articles.heading: Organes du Sénat (1) Les organes du Sénat sont les suivants
Membres de l’Assemblée plénière L’Assemblée plénière se compose de tous les sénateurs
articles.text: Section 2 : Conférence des présidents

articles.heading: Membres de la Conférence des présidents La Conférence des présidents se compose des membres du Bureau du Sénat et des membres
articles.text:
des bureaux des commissions permanentes.
Section 3 : Bureau du Sénat

articles.heading: Membres du Bureau du Sénat Le Bureau du Sénat se compose d’un Président et de deux Vice-présidents élus parmi les
articles.text:
membres du Sénat. Un des Vice-présidents est
chargé des affaires parlementaires et l’autre de
l’administration et des finances.

articles.heading: Élection et prestation de serment des membres du Bureau du Sénat (1) Au début de chaque mandat des sénateurs,
articles.text:
la première séance est consacrée à
l’élection du Bureau du Sénat. Cette séance
est convoquée et présidée par le Président
de la République dans les 30 jours à
compter de la proclamation définitive des
résultats électoraux des sénateurs élus.
(2) L’élection des membres du Bureau du
Sénat a lieu au scrutin secret et à la majorité
absolue des voix des sénateurs présents à la
séance. Chaque membre du Bureau est élu
au scrutin distinct. Si aucun candidat à la
qualité de membre du Bureau n’obtient la
majorité requise, il est procédé à un
nouveau tour de scrutin.
(3) En l’absence de la majorité absolue des
voix au second tour, le candidat qui obtient
le plus grand nombre de voix est réputé élu.
(4) Avant leur entrée en fonction, les membres
du Bureau du Sénat prêtent publiquement,
devant le Président de la République, le
serment prévu par la Constitution de la
République du Rwanda.
(5) Les membres du Bureau du Sénat ont un
mandat de cinq ans.
Section 4 : Commissions permanentes

articles.heading: Commissions permanentes Le Sénat compte les quatre commissions permanentes suivantes
Membres d’une commission permanente et modalités de leur affectation (1) Chaque Commission permanente se
articles.text:
compose d’au moins quatre membres.
(2) Les sénateurs sont affectés à la commission
permanente selon les modalités suivantes :
(a) chaque sénateur se fait inscrire dans
une seule commission permanente ;
(b) Le Bureau du Sénat vérifie les
inscriptions effectuées par les sénateurs
et confirme la composition de chaque
commission permanente, compte tenu
des critères suivants :
(i) préférence exprimée par chaque
sénateur ;
(ii) nombre de membres de chaque
commission permanente ;
(iii) attributions de la commission
permanente ;
(iv) pertinence des qualifications du
sénateur au regard des attributions
de la Commission permanente ;
(v) l’expérience professionnelle du
sénateur en rapport avec les
attributions de la commission
permanente ;
(vi) le principe d’égalité entre femmes
et hommes.
(3) Après l’expiration d’une période de deux
ans et demi, un sénateur qui le désire peut
solliciter le changement de son affectation
au sein d’une commission. L’examen de
cette demande se fait selon la manière
prévue au paragraphe (2) du présent article.
(4) Le Bureau du Sénat peut, dans l’intérêt du
service, réaffecter un sénateur d’une
commission permanente à l’autre.

articles.heading: Bureau de la commission permanente et son élection (1) Chaque commission permanente est dotée
articles.text:
de son propre bureau composé d’un
président et d’un vice-président.
(2) Le président et le vice-président de la
commission permanente sont élus par
l’Assemblée plénière à la majorité absolue
des sénateurs présents à la séance plénière.
Les membres de la commission
permanente souhaitant faire acte de
candidature notifient celle-ci par écrit au
Président du Sénat qui, à son tour, en
informe l’Assemblée plénière.
(3) Le président et le vice-président de la
commission permanente sont élus aux
scrutins distincts.
(4) Si aucun candidat au bureau d’une
commission permanente n’obtient le
nombre de voix requis, il est procédé à un
nouveau scrutin.
(5) En l’absence de majorité absolue de voix
au second tour, le candidat qui obtient le
plus grand nombre de voix est réputé élu.

articles.heading: Mandat et modalités de remplacement des membres du bureau de la commission permanente (1) Les membres du bureau de la commission
articles.text:
permanente exercent leurs fonctions pour
un mandat de deux ans et demi,
renouvelable.
(2) L’un ou les deux membres du bureau de la
commission permanente peuvent être
remplacés en cas de démission ou à la
demande des deux tiers des membres de la
commission permanente. Un avis écrit de
démission ou de demande de
remplacement est adressé au Président du
Sénat.
(3) À la demande des deux tiers des membres
de la commission permanente, le
Président du Sénat renvoie la question au
Comité pour examen.
(4) Le rapport de la commission permanente
sur l’examen de la question concernant le
remplacement du bureau ou de l’un de ses
membres est présenté à l’Assemblée
plénière dans un délai ne dépassant pas
sept jours, pour décision.
(5) Lorsque le bureau de la commission
permanente ou l’un de ses membres
démissionne, ou lorsque l’Assemblée
plénière décide de son remplacement, il
est pourvu au remplacement selon la
manière prévue à l’article 21 de la
présente loi organique, dans les 15 jours à
compter de la date de remise de la
démission au Président du Sénat ou de
celle d’approbation par l’Assemblée
plénière de leur remplacement.

articles.heading: Création d’une commission spéciale À la demande du Président du Sénat, formulée après consultation avec les autres membres du
articles.text:
Bureau du Sénat, ou à la demande d’au moins
cinq sénateurs, et avec l’approbation de
l’Assemblée plénière, le Sénat crée une
commission ad hoc chargée d’examiner un
projet ou proposition de loi ou une quelconque
question particulière.

articles.heading: Élection des membres d’une commission spéciale et de son bureau (1) Les candidats à la qualité de membres
articles.text:
d’une commission spéciale sont proposés
par le Bureau du Sénat et approuvés en
bloc par l’Assemblée plénière à la majorité
absolue des voix des sénateurs présents à la
séance.
(2) Parmi les membres approuvés de la
commission spéciale, le Bureau du Sénat
propose à l’Assemblée plénière les
membres du Bureau de cette commission,
dont un président et un vice-président, pour
approbation par l’Assemblée plénière,
chacun étant approuvé séparément à la
majorité absolue des voix des sénateurs
présents à la séance.
(3) Lorsque l’Assemblée plénière n’approuve
pas les membres d’une commission
spéciale ou l’un ou les deux membres de
son bureau, le Bureau du Sénat propose de
nouveaux candidats pour approbation lors
de la séance plénière suivante.
Section 5 : Comité

articles.heading: Membres et bureau du Comité (1) Le Comité se compose d’au moins cinq sénateurs, proposés par le Bureau du Sénat
articles.text:
pour approbation par l’Assemblée
plénière.
(2) Le Comité est doté d’un bureau composé
d’un président et d’un vice-président, élus
par l’Assemblée plénière conformément
aux dispositions de l’article 21 de la
présente loi organique.

articles.heading: Cumul d’appartenance au Comité et aux commissions permanentes Les sénateurs membres du Comité conservent
articles.text:
leur appartenance aux commissions
permanentes. Toutefois, le président et le viceprésident du Comité ne peuvent faire partie du
Bureau d’aucune commission permanente.

articles.heading: Mandat et modalités de remplacement des membres du bureau du Comité (1) Les membres du bureau du Comité ont un
articles.text:
mandat de deux ans et demi renouvelable.
(2) L’un ou l’autre des membres du bureau du
Comité, ou les deux, peuvent être
remplacés soit en cas de démission, soit à
la demande écrite des deux tiers des
membres du Comité. Une lettre de
démission ou de demande de
remplacement est soumise au Président du
Sénat.
(3) À la demande d’au moins deux tiers des
membres du Comité, le Président du Sénat
renvoie sans délai la question à la
Conférence des présidents pour examen.
En pareil cas, la personne concernée
personnellement par cette question est
priée de se retirer.
(4) Le rapport de la Conférence des présidents
sur l’examen d’une question concernant le
remplacement de l’un ou des deux
membres du Bureau du Comité est
présenté, pour décision, à l’Assemblée
plénière dans les sept jours à compter de sa
soumission à l’Assemblée plénière.
(5) Lorsque l’un ou l’autre membre du Bureau
du Comité, ou les deux, démissionnent ou
lorsque l’Assemblée plénière décide de
procéder à leur remplacement, il est pourvu
audit remplacement selon les modalités
prévues à l’article 21 de la présente loi
organique, dans les 15 jours à compter de
la date de remise de la démission au
Président du Sénat ou de la décision de leur
remplacement prise par l’Assemblée
plénière.
Section 6 : Secrétariat général

articles.heading: Organisation du Secrétariat général (1) Le Secrétariat général du Sénat comprend les services du Sénat chargés d’appuyer
articles.text:
celui-ci dans l’accomplissement de ses
attributions.
(2) Tous les services du Sénat relèvent de
l’autorité du Secrétaire général. Le suivi de
leur fonctionnement est assuré par le
Bureau du Sénat.

articles.heading: Création du cadre organique du Sénat
Nomination du Secrétaire général et du Secrétaire général adjoint Un arrêté présidentiel porte nomination du
articles.text:
Secrétaire général et du Secrétaire général
adjoint.

articles.heading: Recrutement, salaire et avantages du personnel placé sous l’autorité du Secrétariat général
articles.text:
(1) Sous réserve des dispositions de l’article
29 de la présente loi organique, le
personnel placé sous l’autorité du
Secrétariat général est recruté
conformément à la législation en la
matière.
(2) Le salaire et les avantages alloués au
personnel du Sénat sont déterminés
conformément à la législation en la
matière.
CHAPITRE III : FONCTIONNEMENT
DES ORGANES DU SÉNAT
Section première : Attributions et
fonctionnement de l’Assemblée plénière
Sous-section première : Attributions de
l’Assemblée plénière

articles.heading: Attributions de l’Assemblée plénière (1) L’Assemblée plénière est l’organe suprême de décision du Sénat
Sessions ordinaires du Sénat (1) Le Sénat tient trois sessions ordinaires, d’une durée de deux mois chacune
articles.text:
(a) la première session qui s’ouvre le 05
octobre et se clôt le 04 décembre ;
(b) la deuxième session qui s’ouvre le 05
février et se clôt le 04 avril ;
(c) la troisième session qui s’ouvre le 05
juin et se clôt le 04 août.
(2) Lorsque le premier ou le dernier jour d’une
session tombe un jour non ouvrable,
l’ouverture ou la clôture de la session est
reportée au premier jour ouvrable suivant.
(3) Entre les sessions ordinaires, la
Commission permanente poursuit ses
travaux et visites de terrain auprès des
populations.

articles.heading: Convocation d’une session ordinaire Les sénateurs sont convoqués en session ordinaire par le Président du Sénat au moins 15
articles.text:
jours avant la date fixée pour la séance
plénière, au moyen d’un avis écrit remis ou
communiqué aux sénateurs par voie
électronique, par les médias ou par tout autre
moyen de communication.
Cet avis écrit comprend le projet de
programme des travaux de cette session. Il est
communiqué au Président de la République, au
Président de la Chambre des Députés et au
Premier Ministre.

articles.heading: Programme des travaux de la session ordinaire Lors de la première réunion de la session ordinaire, l’Assemblée plénière adopte le
articles.text:
programme des travaux de l’ensemble de la
session.

articles.heading: Présentation à l’Assemblée plénière d’un aperçu des travaux réalisés au cours de la session ordinaire
articles.text:
À la clôture de la session ordinaire, le Président
du Sénat présente à l’Assemblée plénière un
bref aperçu des travaux réalisés par le Sénat au
cours de ladite session.

articles.heading: Convocation d’une session extraordinaire (1) Le Président du Sénat peut, après consultation avec les autres membres du
articles.text:
Bureau du Sénat, convoquer l’Assemblée
plénière en session extraordinaire, ou à la
demande du Président de la République ou
d’un quart des sénateurs.
(2) La session extraordinaire est limitée à
l’examen des questions pour lesquelles elle
a été convoquée et qui ont été
communiquées aux sénateurs avant son
ouverture.
(3) La session extraordinaire a une durée
maximale de 15 jours.

articles.heading: Modalités de convocation d’une session extraordinaire (1) Les sénateurs sont convoqués en session
articles.text:
extraordinaire par le Président du Sénat au
moyen d’un avis écrit qui leur est remis ou
communiqué par voie électronique, par les
médias ou par tout autre moyen de
communication.
(2) L’avis écrit de convocation des sénateurs
en session extraordinaire comprend le
projet de programme des travaux de cette
session extraordinaire et une copie de cet
avis est transmise au Président de la
République et au Premier Ministre.
(3) L’Assemblée plénière délibère uniquement
sur les points inscrits au programme des
travaux de la session extraordinaire et en
décide.

articles.heading: Période de congé officiel pour sénateurs (1) Sous réserve des dispositions de l’article 33 de la présente loi organique, chaque
articles.text:
sénateur bénéficie, chaque année, d’une
période de congé officiel de 30 jours
calendaires, à prendre durant l’intervalle
entre la troisième session ordinaire et la
première session.
(2) L’Assemblée plénière a compétence
exclusive pour fixer le début et la fin de
ladite période de congé officiel.
(3) Le congé officiel peut être pris en une
seule période continue ou répartie en
plusieurs périodes distinctes déterminées
par l’Assemblée plénière.
(4) En cas de motifs justifiant la nonapplication des dispositions du
paragraphe (1) du présent article,
l’Assemblée plénière peut fixer une autre
période pour le début du congé officiel.
(5) Une session extraordinaire peut, en cas de
besoin, être convoquée pendant la période
de congé officiel.
Sous-section 3 : Tenue de la séance plénière

articles.heading: Heures des travaux de l’Assemblée plénière (1) Les travaux de l’Assemblée plénière s’ouvrent à 15 heures et sont levés à 18
articles.text:
heures. Toutefois, le Bureau du Sénat peut
changer l’heure d’ouverture des travaux, à
condition que la durée de ces travaux ne
puisse excéder trois heures.
(2) L’heure de levée de la séance plénière
peut, à la demande du président de séance
plénière, être changée avec l’approbation
des sénateurs présents à la séance, donnée
par consensus. En cas d’absence de
consensus, le changement est décidé à la
majorité absolue des voix des sénateurs
présents à la séance.
(3) Toutefois, lorsque l’heure de levée des
travaux de la séance arrive alors qu’une
personne à qui est donnée la parole n’a pas
encore terminé son intervention, le
président de séance attend la fin de son
intervention avant de solliciter la
prolongation.

articles.heading: Lieu de tenue de la séance plénière (1) La séance plénière du Sénat se tient, sauf cas de force majeure constaté par la Cour
articles.text:
suprême à la demande du Président du
Sénat, au palais du Sénat, situé dans la
capitale de la République du Rwanda.
Lorsque la Cour Suprême est elle-même
dans l’impossibilité de siéger, le Président
de la République détermine, par décret-loi,
le lieu de tenue de la séance.
(2) Le Sénat rend publique la décision visée au
paragraphe (1) du présent article par des
moyens électroniques, par les médias ou
par tout autre moyen de communication.

articles.heading: Tenue et quorum de la séance plénière (1) Pour qu’une séance plénière soit valablement tenue, elle doit se dérouler
articles.text:
dans le palais prévu à cet effet, être
convoquée sur avis, se tenir sur la base
d’un ordre du jour, avoir lieu au cours
d’une session et réunir au moins les trois
cinquièmes des sénateurs.
(2) La séance plénière ne peut se tenir que si
au moins deux membres du Bureau du
Sénat sont présents.
(3) À chaque séance plénière, chaque
sénateur enregistre sa présence en signant
en regard de son nom sur la liste des
présences ou en l’attestant par voie
électronique. Avant l’ouverture de la
séance, le président de séance plénière
annonce le nombre de sénateurs présents
à la séance.
(4) Sauf en cas de force majeure tel que visé
à l’article 41 de la présente loi organique,
toute résolution adoptée en séance
plénière en violation des dispositions du
paragraphe (1) du présent article est nulle
et de nul effet.

articles.heading: Principe de publicité des séances plénières (1) Les séances plénières sont publiques
articles.text:
(2) Toutefois, à la demande du Président de
la République, du Président du Sénat, du
Premier Ministre ou d’un quart des
sénateurs, le Sénat peut siéger à huis clos,
à condition que cette demande soit
approuvée par un vote à la majorité
absolue des voix des sénateurs présents à
la séance.
(3) Une décision de tenir une séance plénière
à huis clos fait l’objet d’une publicité par
voie électronique, par les médias ou par
tout autre moyen de communication.

articles.heading: Disposition de sièges dans la salle plénière (1) Les sénateurs se voient attribuer des sièges permanents dans la salle plénière
articles.text:
selon l’ordre alphabétique de leurs noms
tels qu’ils figurent sur la carte nationale
d’identité.
(2) Toutefois, le Bureau du Sénat peut, pour
motif de handicap ou pour toute autre
cause, approuver une dérogation aux
dispositions du paragraphe (1) du présent
article. Cette décision est communiquée à
tous les sénateurs.
(3) Des sièges sont également réservés aux
membres du Bureau du Sénat, aux
représentants du Gouvernement ainsi qu’à
d’autres personnes participant aux travaux
de l’Assemblée plénière.

articles.heading: Programme hebdomadaire des travaux de l’Assemblée plénière (1) Le projet de programme hebdomadaire des
articles.text:
travaux de l’Assemblée plénière est établi
par le Secrétaire général sur la base des
points inscrits au programme des travaux
de la session et soumis au Bureau du Sénat
pour approbation.
(2) L’ordre du jour des travaux de l’Assemblée
plénière est transmis aux sénateurs au
moins deux jours avant l’examen, par la
séance plénière, des points qui y sont
inscrits, sauf en cas d’urgence. Cet ordre du
jour est rendu public par voie électronique,
par les médias ou par tout autre moyen de
communication.

articles.heading: Délai de transmission aux sénateurs d’un document appelé à être examiné en séance plénière Un document comportant des points appelés à
articles.text:
